Same head-gasket/overheating and sludging pattern carried over from the WJ.

TIPM-7 Totally Integrated Power Module internal fuel-pump relay sticks or fails, causing stalling, no-start, and fuel pump running with the key off. Addressed by NHTSA recall 15V-115 with an external relay bypass.

Left-bank cylinder head valve-guide wear causes exhaust valve sealing loss and misfire (DTCs P0302/P0304/P0306) with a driver-side ticking noise. Not a safety recall — covered by TSB 09-002-14 and Chrysler warranty extension X56 (10 yr / 150k mi).

Monostable electronic gear selector gives no tactile or visual confirmation of the selected gear; drivers exited with the vehicle still in gear, producing rollaway crashes. Recalled 2016 (NHTSA 16V-240) across ~1.1M FCA vehicles; linked to 266 crashes and 68 injuries.
Quadra-Lift air suspension compressor and height-sensor failures causing the vehicle to sag or refuse to change ride height.
EGR cooler cracking and emissions-system faults; the 2014-2016 EcoDiesel was also subject to the FCA diesel emissions consent decree and recalibration.

engines: 2.0L GME turbo I4 in the 4xe plug-in hybrid (375 hp combined)

known_issues.description: High-voltage battery pack defects prompted fire-risk recalls with a do-not-charge / park-outside advisory on 4xe models shared with the Wrangler 4xe.
Uconnect 5 software faults producing blank screens, rearview-camera image loss and instrument-cluster dropouts; multiple software recalls.

generations.mixed_year_note: Both the outgoing and incoming generation were sold in this model year; NHTSA records do not separate them.

notes: The Silverado NAMEPLATE on the 1500 begins with MY1999. NHTSA 'SILVERADO 1500' records for MY1996-1998 are the GMT400 C/K 1500, on which 'Silverado' was a trim level — these must be treated as a separate pre-nameplate generation, not folded into the GMT800 page. One genuine MY OVERLAP: for MY2007 GM sold both the new GMT900 and a carryover GMT800 badged 'Silverado 1500 Classic', so 2007 complaint records span two platforms and must be split by VIN/body, not year. A softer overlap exists at MY2019, where the K2XX continued as the 'Silverado 1500 LD' alongside the new T1XX. Mid-generation powertrain boundaries that matter more than the generation split: AFM cylinder deactivation arrives with the GMT900 in 2007, the 8L90 8-speed arrives mid-K2XX (2015 on 6.2L, 2016 on 5.3L), and DFM replaces AFM on the T1XX.

known_issues.description: 4L60E 3-4 clutch pack and sun-shell failures causing loss of 3rd/4th gear.
Central port injection (CPI/'spider') fuel injector poppet leaks on the 4.3L V6 causing hard starting and rough running.
Cab-corner, rocker-panel and rear wheel-arch rust in salt-belt use.
Stepper-motor failure in the gauge cluster causing gauges to stick, read wrong or drop to zero; the fuel-level sender also fails from sulfur deposits.
ABS wheel-speed sensor and EBCM faults causing unwanted low-speed ABS activation and extended stopping distance; subject of NHTSA recall action on 1999-2002 GM trucks.
Intermediate steering shaft wear producing a clunk or knock on turn-in; a very high-volume TSB item.
4L60E clutch pack and sun-shell failures, worsened by towing.

Excessive oil consumption on Gen IV 5.3L AFM engines — the AFM oil pressure relief valve sprays oil at the piston skirts while low-tension piston rings fail to control it, fouling plugs and dropping oil level between changes. Subject of the Siqueiros v. GM class action covering the LC9 5.3L in 2011-2014 trucks and SUVs.
Collapsed AFM lifters on the deactivating cylinders, often wiping the corresponding camshaft lobe; presents as a misfire plus a persistent top-end tick.
Dashboard top-pad cracking and splitting, widespread enough to generate its own complaint category.

generations.mixed_year_note: Both the outgoing and incoming generation were sold in this model year; NHTSA records do not separate them.

known_issues.description: Torque-converter shudder and harsh 2-3 / 3-4 shifts traced to the original Dexron-VI fluid formulation; GM's fix was a flush to Mobil 1 Dexron HP fluid, with repeat failures common. Same defect family as the 8L45.
AFM lifter collapse on the deactivating cylinders, frequently taking out the camshaft; owner reports cluster around 100k-120k miles.
Continued excessive oil consumption on the Gen V L83, from piston-ring sealing and AFM oil management.
A/C condenser and evaporator leaks causing loss of cooling, a high-volume complaint on this body.

Connecting-rod and main bearing failure causing sudden engine seizure or loss of power; GM recalled roughly 597,000 2021-2024 trucks and SUVs with the 6.2L L87 in April 2025, attributing it to manufacturing debris and bearing/crankshaft dimensional variation.
Dynamic Fuel Management lifter failure — the same deactivating-lifter mechanism as AFM, extended to more cylinders; produces misfire and camshaft lobe damage.
Shudder, harsh 1-2 shifts and torque-converter complaints, addressed by fluid and control-module recalibration TSBs.

notes: US-market split; the Altima nameplate is US/North-America specific (the contemporaneous global car is the Teana/Bluebird Sylphy family, which does not share this generation timeline). Generations are contiguous with no gaps. The most important boundary for a reliability site is not a generation edge but a mid-history powertrain change: JATCO CVTs replace the conventional automatic from MY2007 (L32), and from MY2013 (L33) the CVT is the only transmission offered. The Altima Hybrid (2007-2011) used a Toyota-licensed HSD powertrain and behaves as a distinct sub-population inside the L32.

known_issues.description: KA24DE timing chain guide wear producing a rattle at cold start.
Timing chain guide and tensioner wear on the KA24DE; distributor and crankshaft position sensor failures causing intermittent stalling and no-start.
Catalytic converter and oxygen sensor failures generating high check-engine-light complaint volume.

Pre-catalyst substrate breaks down and ceramic particles are drawn back into the cylinders through the exhaust valves, scoring bores and causing runaway oil consumption and eventual engine failure. Nissan extended emissions warranty coverage on affected cars.
Head gasket failure, often after the pre-cat/oil-consumption sequence above.
Crankshaft position sensor and camshaft position sensor failures causing stall-while-driving; a large NHTSA complaint cluster.

engines: 2.5L Atkinson I4 + Toyota-licensed hybrid system (Altima Hybrid, 2007-2011)

known_issues.description: JATCO Xtronic CVT overheating and belt/pulley failure producing judder, delayed engagement and loss of drive. Nissan extended CVT coverage to 10 years / 120,000 miles on affected 2007-2010 CVT vehicles.
ESCL module failure leaves the steering locked and the vehicle unable to start; addressed by recall and warranty extension.
Elevated oil consumption complaints continuing from the L31 QR25DE family.

transmissions: JATCO CVT8 (RE0F10D / JF016E) — no manual offered

known_issues.description: CVT8 shuddering, hesitation, surging and premature failure — overheated fluid lets the steel belt slip on the pulleys and shed metal debris. Class action settled for MY2013-2016 Altimas with warranty extension to 84 months / 84,000 miles plus repair reimbursement; Nissan set aside $590.5M to extend CVT warranties from 5 to 7 years across ~3M vehicles.
Secondary hood latch corrosion could allow the hood to fly open while driving; recalled on 2013-2015 cars.
Continued CVT judder and hesitation complaints, though at materially lower rates than the L33; the CVT remains the dominant complaint category for the generation.
The variable-compression multi-link actuator mechanism adds failure surface not present on the 2.5L; the engine was withdrawn after MY2023.

notes: CRITICAL GAP: in the US market the Cherokee nameplate is absent for MY2002-2013. The XJ ended after MY2001; its replacement (KJ 2002-2007, KK 2008-2012) was sold in the US as the Jeep LIBERTY and appears in NHTSA under that model name, so those records must NOT be merged into a Cherokee page even though the rest of the world called them Cherokee. MY2013 has no US Cherokee or Liberty at all — the Liberty ended after MY2012 and the KL arrived for MY2014. This is exactly the boundary that would silently fuse an XJ body-on-unibody 4x4 with a transverse-engine crossover. A sixth generation (KM) resumes at MY2026, outside the 1996-2023 NHTSA span given.

known_issues.description: Cylinder heads with casting number 0331 crack between the #3 exhaust valve seat and the pushrod hole, causing coolant loss into the cylinder and overheating. Affects late 4.0L heads.
'Death wobble' — self-sustaining front-axle oscillation triggered by a bump, from worn track bar, ball joints, tie rods and steering damper.
Closed-cooling-system radiators, fan clutches and plastic end tanks fail, and the 4.0L is intolerant of the resulting overheating.
Severe rust in floor pans, rear quarter panels, and the unibody rails behind the rear wheels.

Harsh and erratic shifting, hard downshifts and unexpected drops into neutral. FCA maintained the root cause was control software and issued multiple recalls and software patches; a 2016 recall (NHTSA 16V-529) covered 2014 models with the 3.2L V6 where a sticking valve could prevent a clutch from disengaging and force a shift to neutral. 2014-2015 models alone generated over 7,000 transmission complaints, ~4,000 of them on MY2014.
Excessive oil consumption from piston-ring sealing loss, in some cases progressing to low-oil engine damage.
Power transfer unit (PTU) and rear drive module failures on 4x4 models producing whine, vibration and loss of drive.

production_gaps.reason: US market gap — no Cherokee sold (sold as Jeep Liberty KJ/KK, a separate NHTSA nameplate; no successor at all for MY2013)

notes: US-market model years. No gaps — the US split is 1996-2000 / 2001-2005 / 2006-2012 / 2013-2018 / 2019-2025, with a sixth generation (XA60) arriving for MY2026 outside the NHTSA span given. Note that Toyota's global XA20 and XA30 timelines run a year off the US ones in some references (the XA30 launched globally in late 2005 as a MY2006 US car), so a source saying '2005' for the third generation is describing production start, not US model year. The first-generation RAV4 EV (1997-2003) and the Tesla-powertrain RAV4 EV (2012-2014) are separate low-volume vehicles and appear in NHTSA under 'RAV4 EV'; do not merge them with the gasoline RAV4.

known_issues.description: Viscous coupling / center differential wear on full-time 4WD models causing binding on turns.

ECM failure corrupts the shift solenoid control signals, producing violent harsh shifting, gear hunting and eventual transaxle damage. Toyota issued a nationwide warranty enhancement in 2010 covering the ECM and, where needed, the transaxle for 10 years / 150,000 miles, keyed to DTCs P0750, P0753, P0755, P0758 and P1760.
Cylinder-head threads for the head bolts strip on early 2AZ-FE builds; also the start of the 2AZ oil-consumption pattern.

Excessive oil consumption caused by piston-ring design allowing oil past the rings; owners report losing a quart per 1,000 miles or less. Toyota's warranty enhancement covered 2006-2008 RAV4s for 10 years / 150,000 miles with a revised piston assembly.
Rear suspension arm corrosion in salt-belt states could allow the arm to separate; subject of a Toyota recall covering 2006-2011 RAV4s.
Intermediate steering shaft wear producing a clunk and, in some cases, notchy steering feel.
Denso low-pressure fuel pump impeller cracking causing stalling; the recall population extends into MY2018-2019 RAV4s.
No dominant systemic mechanical defect — this generation is the reliability high-water mark of the nameplate; complaint volume is concentrated in infotainment, HVAC and paint rather than powertrain.
Denso low-pressure fuel pump impeller cracks and swells, seizing the pump and causing engine stall without warning; recalled in 2019 and expanded in 2020 across a large Toyota population.
Harsh, hesitant and clunky low-speed shifting and delayed engagement, addressed by control-module recalibration TSBs.
AWD models will not accept a full tank of fuel from the pump's automatic shutoff, an acknowledged tank-geometry limitation rather than a defect fix.
12-volt battery hold-down clamp allows the battery to shift and short against the hood, a fire risk; recalled on 2019-2020 vehicles.

notes: US-market model years, which run one year later than the production years quoted in most references (e.g. the B15 entered production in 1999 but is a MY2000 US car; the B16 entered production in 2006 but is a MY2007 US car). The B17-to-B18 boundary is the one most often reported wrong: MY2019 is the LAST B17 and MY2020 is the FIRST B18 — verified against multiple sources. A ninth generation (B19) arrives for MY2026, outside the span. As with the Altima, the decisive reliability boundary is the arrival of the JATCO CVT at MY2007.

known_issues.description: Distributor and crank/cam position sensor failures causing intermittent stalling and no-start.

engines: 2.5L QR25DE I4 (165-175 hp, SE-R and SE-R Spec V, 2002-2006)

known_issues.description: Pre-catalyst substrate disintegrates and ceramic debris is drawn back into the cylinders, scoring bores and producing runaway oil consumption and engine failure — the same mechanism as the contemporaneous Altima 2.5.
Catalytic converter and oxygen sensor failures plus excessive oil consumption at higher mileage.
Crankshaft position sensor failures causing stall-while-driving.

engines: 2.5L QR25DE I4 (177-200 hp, SE-R and SE-R Spec V)

known_issues.description: CVT fluid-temperature protection logic derates the vehicle after sustained high-speed or uphill operation in hot ambient conditions (documented at roughly 4000+ rpm and 65+ mph above ~96 F), and belt/pulley failures follow overheating. Nissan extended CVT coverage to 10 years / 120,000 miles on affected 2007-2010 vehicles.
Timing chain guide wear and elevated oil consumption at higher mileage.

engines: 1.6L MR16DDT turbo I4 (188-and-up hp, SR Turbo and NISMO, 2017-2019)

known_issues.description: JATCO RE0F11A judder, shudder at light throttle, hesitation and premature failure. Valve-body bore wear causes line-pressure leakage and sticking solenoids; P0741 torque-converter-lockup and related judder codes are the signature. Nissan extended the original 5-year / 60,000-mile CVT warranty to 7 years / 84,000 miles for many of these cars.
Elevated oil consumption and timing-chain noise complaints at higher mileage.

No widely documented systemic powertrain defect as of MY2025; the CVT and engine complaint rates fall sharply relative to the B17, and this generation is a deliberate reset of the Sentra's CVT reputation.

notes: US-market only; the Cruze went on sale in the US for MY2011 (it existed globally from 2009). One genuine MY OVERLAP at 2016: GM sold the all-new J400 'Cruze' alongside a carryover J300 badged 'Cruze Limited' for the whole 2016 model year, so MY2016 NHTSA records under 'CRUZE' contain two entirely different cars on two different platforms. Split MY2016 by VIN or by the 'Limited' designation — the 1.4L LUJ/LUV (J300) and 1.4L LE2 (J400) have different failure profiles. I have assigned MY2016 to the second generation and flagged the Limited here rather than creating an overlapping range. US production ended March 2019; the Cruze continued in Argentina to 2023 but those cars are not in NHTSA data.

generations.gen_label: 1st generation (J300) — plus the MY2016 'Cruze Limited' carryover

known_issues.description: The PCV regulator diaphragm integrated into the plastic valve cover ruptures, and the intake-manifold check valve and corrugated PCV hose fail alongside it, creating an uncontrolled vacuum leak. Symptoms are a whistle, rough idle, oil consumption, and in severe cases the crankcase vacuum blows out the rear main seal. All three components are known weak points across MY2011-2016.

Coolant/water outlet housing and thermostat housing crack and leak (commonly seen dripping under the throttle body onto the transmission); water pump leaks are also frequent and were covered to 10 years / 120,000 miles.

Negative battery cable terminal was under-crimped at the factory and loosens over time, raising internal resistance. Produces flickering lights, radio/HVAC display cycling, and spurious ABS / Service Traction / Service StabiliTrak / power-steering messages, and can cause stalling. Covered by GM Special Coverage 14311 and Customer Satisfaction Program 46000, extended to 10 years / 120,000 miles.
Wastegate and turbo bearing failures on the 1.4L LUJ producing loss of boost and a check-engine light.
Coolant leaks from the plastic thermostat/water-outlet housing and turbo coolant lines, plus continued PCV-system and valve-cover failures inherited in concept from the LUJ.
Head gasket failure and coolant loss reported at moderate mileage, often following the cooling-system leaks above.
DEF/SCR and DPF regeneration faults triggering limp mode and no-start countdowns.

notes: IMPORTANT DATA ARTIFACT: the NHTSA span of 1996-2010 for make DODGE / model RAM 1500 does NOT mean the truck ended in 2010. The Ram brand was split from Dodge for MY2011, so MY2011 and later records for the same vehicle live under make RAM, model 1500. The fourth generation (DS, MY2009-2018) is therefore SPLIT ACROSS TWO NHTSA MAKE RECORDS — 2009-2010 under DODGE, 2011-2018 under RAM. Any generation page must union both or it will show a fourth-gen truck that mysteriously stops in 2010. Secondary caveat: the DS body continued to be sold as the 'Ram 1500 Classic' for MY2019-2024 alongside the fifth-generation DT, another two-platforms-one-model-year overlap (under the RAM make). Also note the 1500's second generation ends at MY2001 while the 2500/3500 ran to MY2002, and the third generation's 1500 ran MY2002-2008 while the HD ran MY2003-2009.

known_issues.description: Widespread failures: governor pressure solenoid and transducer failure causing erratic or 2nd-gear-start shifting, overdrive clutch burnup and slipping. The single largest complaint category for the generation.
Dashboard top-pad cracking and splitting into sharp fragments, exposing wiring.
Ball joint wear on 4WD models and vacuum-actuated front axle disconnect failures preventing 4WD engagement.
Exhaust manifold bolts snap at the head, producing a cold-start 'Hemi tick' and an exhaust leak that worsens as more bolts fail; warped manifold flanges and gasket leaks follow.
Head gasket failure after overheating, plus sludge buildup when oil changes lapse, leading to rocker-arm wear and oil starvation. The 3.7L V6 shares the sludging tendency.
Ball joint wear and 'death wobble' on 4WD models from worn track bar and steering linkage.
Dash pad cracking into sharp pieces that rattle and expose wiring — a defining complaint for this body.
Broken exhaust manifold bolts continue into the DS body; MDS-related lifter and camshaft lobe wear on the deactivating cylinders.

Totally Integrated Power Module internal relay failures causing stalling, no-start, and fuel pump or wiper operation with the key off — the same TIPM family that affected other Chrysler products of the era.
Optional rear coil-spring / air suspension setup: air compressor and height-sensor failures on air-equipped trucks.

notes: US-market. There is NO model-year gap despite the nameplate's discontinuity: the fourth generation ended after MY2007 (production stopped 27 October 2006, final years largely fleet), and the fifth generation began at MY2008 as a facelifted, renamed Ford Five Hundred. Ford numbers 2008-2009 and 2010-2019 as separate generations even though both sit on the D3 platform, because MY2010 was a complete exterior and interior redesign. For a reliability site this is the right split, since the 2008-2009 car is mechanically a Five Hundred while the 2010+ car brings the EcoBoost engines. The Ford Five Hundred (2005-2007) and Taurus X (2008-2009) are separate NHTSA nameplates and must not be merged in. The Taurus SHO name covers two unrelated cars: the 3.4L Yamaha V8 (1996-1999) and the 3.5L EcoBoost (2010-2019).

known_issues.description: Forward clutch and torque-converter hub / input-shaft failures presenting as complete loss of drive engagement with no abnormal noise — engine revs normally, vehicle does not move. One of the highest-volume Ford transmission complaint patterns of the era.
Camshaft sprockets are press-fitted rather than keyed to the camshafts and can slip, destroying valvetrain and pistons. The defining SHO V8 failure mode.
Head gasket failure and coolant contamination, aggravated by rust and scale buildup in the cooling jackets and by overheating.
Coil pack and ignition module failures causing misfire and stalling.
Continued torque-converter, input-shaft and forward-clutch failures producing loss of drive; the AX4N pattern carries directly over from the DN101.
Front coil springs fracture from corrosion and the broken end can puncture the tire, causing loss of control. Subject of NHTSA recall action on salt-belt Taurus and Sable cars of the early 2000s.
Head gasket and intake manifold gasket failures with coolant loss.

transmissions: 6F50 6-speed automatic (replacing the Five Hundred's ZF CFT30 CVT)

known_issues.description: Early 6F50 torque-converter and internal solenoid complaints producing harsh shifts and shudder.

The severe ZF CFT30 CVT failures associated with this body belong to the 2005-2007 Ford Five Hundred, which used the CVT; the Taurus-badged 2008-2009 cars do not have it. Do not attribute CVT failures to this generation.

Internal chain-driven water pump failure dumps coolant directly into the crankcase; the pump is buried in the front of the engine so replacement is an engine-out-scale job. Affects the SHO's 3.5L EcoBoost.
Intake valve carbon buildup on the direct-injected EcoBoost engines causing misfire and rough running, since no port fuel wash cleans the valves.
Door latch pawl spring tab fractures, allowing a door to appear closed but open while driving; subject of a large Ford recall covering 2013-2016 Taurus among other models.
MyFord Touch system freezes, reboots and loses climate/audio control; a very high complaint category for 2011-2015 cars.

notes: US-market model years, contiguous with no gaps: 2005-2009 / 2010-2015 / 2016-2021 / 2022-present. Two naming traps: (1) the second generation was sold as 'ix35' in Europe, Australia and China but kept the Tucson name in the US, so European sources describing an 'ix35' generation are describing the US 2010-2015 Tucson; (2) the third generation returned the Tucson name globally, so US and global generation numbering realign from 2016. The Tucson skipped a US model year at neither boundary — the first generation ran through MY2009 and the second arrived for MY2010. Note also that the Theta II 2.0/2.4 GDI engine problems are usually reported against the Sonata and Santa Fe, but Tucson models with those engines fall inside Hyundai's Theta II engine settlement and KSDS knock-sensor software campaign.

known_issues.description: Crankshaft position sensor and ignition faults causing intermittent stalling and hard starting.
ABS and ESC module faults producing warning lights and, in some reports, unwanted ABS activation at low speed.
No single dominant systemic defect for this generation; complaint volume is spread across stalling, electrical and airbag occupant-classification faults rather than concentrated in one component.

Connecting-rod bearing wear and seizure caused by machining debris left in the crankshaft oil passages restricting oil flow; presents as a knocking noise escalating to engine failure or stall while driving. Covered by Hyundai's Theta II engine settlement and the KSDS knock-sensor detection software campaign, with extended engine warranty coverage.
Stop lamp switch failure causing brake lights not to illuminate, cruise control not to cancel, and push-button start / shifter interlock faults; subject of a broad Hyundai recall.
6-speed automatic harsh shifting and torque-converter shudder complaints.

Clutch application logic causes delayed engagement, hesitation and jerking at low speed, and repeated accelerator pedal cycling in high ambient temperatures can leave the vehicle unable to accelerate at all; owners also report loss of power and stalling. NHTSA recall 16V-628 covered 2016 Tucsons with the 7-speed DCT built 20 May 2015 to 31 May 2016; a class action settled for $41.2 million with a warranty extension and repair reimbursement, and MY2017 cars required a TCM software update.
Connecting-rod bearing wear and seizure from oil-passage debris — the same Theta II mechanism as the LM, covered by the engine settlement and KSDS software campaign.

Electrical short in the ABS hydraulic electronic control unit can ignite even with the vehicle parked and off; Hyundai issued recalls with a park-outside advisory covering 2019-2021 Tucsons among other models.

engines: 1.6L Smartstream T-GDI turbo I4 hybrid (226 hp combined)

known_issues.description: Instrument panel software fault can leave the gauge cluster blank at startup, hiding speed and warning telltales; addressed by a software recall on early NX4 cars.
Low-speed hesitation and shift-shock complaints tied to the idle stop-and-go system and 8-speed automatic calibration.

notes: NHTSA span starts at 2000, but the Escape's first US model year is 2001 (it went on sale in calendar 2000 as a MY2001). Treat any MY2000 records as mis-keyed early-build 2001 cars — do not create a 2000 page. Gen 1 and Gen 2 share the CD2 architecture; Gen 2 (2008-2012) is a heavy restyle plus a new interior and, from 2009, a new powertrain set, and both Ford and every reference source treat it as a separate generation, so keep the pages split. Wikipedia's spec table lists a 'dual-clutch automatic' for the 2013-2019 generation; that is the European Kuga. Every US Escape of that generation used the 6F35 torque-converter 6-speed. The Escape Hybrid is not a separate nameplate in NHTSA data — it lives inside each generation. Gen 4 continues into MY2026 (announced as its final year); the map stops at 2025 to match the data span.

known_issues.description: Texas Instruments speed control deactivation switch mounted in the master cylinder can leak brake fluid onto the switch contacts and ignite, causing an engine-bay fire with the vehicle parked and off. Part of Ford's multi-model speed-control switch recall campaign.
Rear subframe corrodes and can fracture or separate in road-salt states, allowing loss of rear suspension location. Addressed by region-specific inspection/replacement campaigns.
CD4E 4-speed automatic suffers forward clutch and torque converter failures; a common complaint cluster across the generation.
3.0L Duratec V6 intake manifold and coolant crossover leaks leading to overheating.
6F35 6-speed automatic: torque converter shudder, and left-hand halfshaft seal leaks that drain fluid and burn the clutches.
Electronic throttle body failures put the vehicle into reduced-power limp mode without warning.
Electric power steering assist can be lost intermittently, requiring steering gear replacement.

1.6L EcoBoost: if coolant level drops, the cylinder head overheats, cracks and leaks oil onto hot exhaust components, causing underhood fires. Ford ran successive campaigns (12S45, 13S12, 17S09) culminating in fitting a coolant level sensor with warning logic.

1.5L EcoBoost coolant intrusion: coolant migrates from the block into the combustion chamber through the block-to-head interface, causing misfires, white smoke, coolant loss and eventual head cracking or engine failure.
Door latch pawl spring tab can break, so a door may appear shut but can open while driving. Multi-model Ford recall.
Launch-year 1.6L cars had fuel line splitting and multiple other first-year recalls; the 2013 model year is an outlier in recall count even within this generation.

1.5L EcoBoost three-cylinder fuel injectors can crack, leaking fuel and vapor into the cylinder head area near ignition sources, causing underhood fires. Covered by successive recalls (22S43, 22S73, and a 2025 expansion) affecting roughly 850,000 Escape and Bronco Sport vehicles; interim remedy is ECU software that detects a cracked injector.
8F35 8-speed automatic harsh or delayed shifting and shudder complaints.

notes: US model-year boundaries confirmed: Y3 ends MY1998, EF runs MY1999-2005 (US sales Jan 1999 - Jan 2005), NF starts MY2006 as the first US-built Sonata (Montgomery, Alabama). The 2002 'New EF' is a facelift on the same platform, not a new generation — but it does change the V6 from the 2.5L to the 2.7L Delta, which matters for failure patterns. Global sources sometimes number these generations differently (some count the Y2 as second, making the EF the fourth; others make the EF the third). Chassis codes, not ordinal numbers, are the reliable key. The single most important boundary on this nameplate for a reliability site is 2010/2011: the NF's 2.4L Theta is a port-injected engine with no bearing-failure history, while the YF's 2.4L Theta II GDI is the engine at the centre of the recall program. Do not let those two share a page or a failure-mode hub.

known_issues.description: 4-speed automatic failures are the dominant complaint; these are Mitsubishi-derived drivetrains from Hyundai's pre-in-house-engine era.
Interference-design belt-driven engines: a snapped timing belt causes valve-to-piston contact.
2.7L Delta V6 is belt-driven and interference-design; belt service neglect causes valve damage.
Rear subframe and control arm corrosion in road-salt states.

The 2.4L Theta here is the port-injected version, NOT the Theta II GDI. It has no connecting-rod-bearing recall history — an important distinction from the 2011+ car that shares the '2.4 Theta' shorthand.
Occupant classification / passenger airbag sensing system faults leading to non-deployment conditions; subject to campaign action.

Theta II GDI connecting-rod bearing failure: metallic debris left in the crankshaft oil passages during machining migrates into the connecting-rod oil feeds, restricting oil flow to the bearings. Result is knocking, power loss, bearing seizure, engine stall at speed, and in some cases a punctured block with an oil fire. Recall 15V-568 covered MY2011-2012 2.0L and 2.4L Theta II GDI Sonatas; recall 17V-226 extended it to MY2013-2014.
Knock Sensor Detection System software campaign later applied across Theta II GDI cars to detect incipient bearing failure and put the engine into limp mode before seizure.
Electric power steering / steering column coupler complaints producing sudden loss of assist.

Theta II GDI connecting-rod bearing wear and seizure continues into this generation. Hyundai extended engine warranty coverage and applied the Knock Sensor Detection System software campaign across MY2011-2019 Theta II GDI vehicles.
7-speed dual-clutch behind the 1.6L turbo: low-speed shudder, hesitation from a stop, and clutch wear.
ABS hydraulic control unit can short internally and ignite while parked; subject to recall with an interim instruction to park outdoors.
Trims without an engine immobilizer are trivially hot-wired, producing a large theft loss pattern and insurer refusals. Hyundai issued a software countermeasure rather than a recall.

notes: There is a hard one-model-year gap: the HB generation ends after MY2009 and the WK2-based generation starts at MY2011. No US MY2010 Durango exists — any MY2010 record is a data error. The other structural break is architectural, not just cosmetic: gens 1 and 2 are body-on-frame Dakota-derived trucks, while gen 3 is a unibody crossover sharing the Jeep Grand Cherokee WK2 platform (Mercedes M-Class derived). Those should never share a failure-mode page. Gen 3 is exceptionally long-running (15+ model years) and has two major mid-generation powertrain shifts worth surfacing on the page even though they do not create a new generation: the ZF 8-speed replacing the 5-speeds from MY2014, and the arrival of the SRT V8s from MY2018.

known_issues.description: Upper ball joint wear and separation causing loss of steering control; subject to recall on the Durango/Dakota chassis.
4.7L PowerTech V8 head gasket and cylinder head cracking following overheating; the engine has little margin once coolant is lost.
46RE overdrive clutch and governor pressure solenoid failures.
5.7L Hemi with MDS cylinder deactivation: camshaft lobe and roller lifter wear producing a tick, then metal in the oil and bottom-end damage.
Hemi exhaust manifold bolt breakage causing an exhaust leak with a cold-start tick.
Totally Integrated Power Module faults producing no-start, stalling and phantom electrical behaviour.
4.7L V8 valve seat and head issues carried over from the previous generation.

generations.platform_code: WD (shares Jeep Grand Cherokee WK2 architecture)

known_issues.description: 3.6L Pentastar left-bank cylinder head: valve seat erosion and valve guide wear, classically showing as a driver's-side tick with a cylinder 2 misfire (P0302), and in severe cases an exhaust valve dropping into the cylinder. Chrysler handled it with TSB 09-002-14 and warranty extension X56 (10 years / 150,000 miles) rather than a safety recall.
TIPM-7 (Totally Integrated Power Module) failures: no-start, stalling in traffic, fuel pump running with the key off, and unintended accessory operation.
Alternator failure on 3.6L cars causing sudden loss of electrical power and stalling; subject to recall.
5.7L Hemi MDS roller lifter and camshaft lobe failure — the dominant V8 failure mode across the whole generation.
Early ZF 8-speed installations had shift-quality and calibration problems addressed through repeated software flashes.

notes: 'Grand Caravan' is the long-wheelbase body; the short-wheelbase 'Caravan' is a separate NHTSA model name and should not be merged in. The nameplate ends in the US after MY2020 — the last van was built 21 August 2020. The 2021 'Grand Caravan' was a Canada-only Chrysler-badged rebadge of the Voyager and is not a US vehicle, so the NHTSA span ending at 2020 is correct and the map should not be extended. The RT generation runs 13 model years, which is long enough that the page needs an internal split marker: MY2011 brought a full powertrain replacement (3.6L Pentastar for the 3.3/3.8/4.0 V6s, 62TE standard) plus a new interior. That is a facelift by platform definition but it changes essentially every failure mode, so treat 2008-2010 and 2011-2020 as distinct cohorts within one generation page.

known_issues.description: 41TE / A604 Ultradrive automatic failure is the signature defect of this generation: solenoid pack faults, planetary and clutch pack failure, often well before 100,000 miles.
3.3L and 3.8L head gasket and intake plenum gasket leaks causing coolant loss and overheating.
41TE automatic failures continue as the leading complaint category.
Power sliding door motor, cable and latch failures — doors that fail to latch, open on their own, or jam.

TIPM-7 fuel pump relay failure: the internal relay contacts degrade, causing intermittent no-start, stalling while driving, and the fuel pump continuing to run with the key off. One of the most-complained-about defects in NHTSA's database for this vehicle.
3.6L Pentastar left-bank cylinder head valve guide and valve seat wear (driver's side tick, cylinder 2 misfire), covered by Chrysler warranty extension X56 rather than a recall.
The ignition switch can move out of the RUN position while driving, shutting off the engine and disabling the airbags; subject to recall.
Power sliding door and power liftgate motor, cable and wiring harness failures persist across the whole generation.

notes: No gaps and no overlaps — the four generations tile 2005-2025 cleanly. Two cautions for data grouping. First, the Equinox EV (2024 onward, Ultium BEV) is a completely different vehicle that in some feeds carries the same 'EQUINOX' model name; check for a fuel-type or VIN discriminator before folding those records into the gen 3/gen 4 pages. Second, gens 1 and 2 are both nominally 'Theta' but are not the same car in any way that matters: gen 1 is the Canadian-built 3.4L V6 vehicle, gen 2 is the 2.4L Ecotec four-cylinder vehicle whose oil-consumption defect dominates its complaint record. The 2.4L Ecotec oil consumption story is the single highest-value failure-mode hub on this nameplate: GM issued per-model-year Special Coverage adjustments and settled a class action for MY2010-2013, while later suits allege MY2014-2017 cars share the identical defect — state both facts, since the settlement year range and the defect year range differ.

known_issues.description: 3.4L V6 intake manifold and head gasket coolant leaks leading to overheating and head damage.
3.6L LY7 timing chain stretch producing P0008/P0016 cam-crank correlation codes and a cold-start rattle.
Aisin AF33 5-speed automatic failures, often expensive because of limited rebuild support.

2.4L Ecotec excessive oil consumption: the piston and piston ring assembly does not maintain adequate ring tension, so oil passes into the combustion chamber. The resulting chronic low oil level causes timing chain wear and connecting rod bearing failure. GM issued Special Coverage adjustments per model year and a class action settlement (final approval November 2019) covered MY2010-2013 Equinox and GMC Terrain; subsequent suits allege MY2014-2017 units have the same defect without the same coverage.
2.4L timing chain stretch, frequently secondary to the oil consumption defect above.
1.5L LYX oil consumption and PCV system diaphragm failure, which draws oil into the intake and can damage the turbocharger.
Intake valve carbon buildup inherent to the port-less direct injection design, causing misfires and rough idle at higher mileage.
9T50 9-speed automatic shift quality and calibration complaints.

build_notes: n/a: Too new for any systemic defect pattern to be established in the complaint record. The move to a CVT on front-drive cars is the notable engineering change to watch.

notes: Two boundary hazards. First, the NHTSA span starts at 2002 but the US Sorento's first model year is 2003 — the 2002 date reflects the Korean launch. Treat MY2002 records as stray. Second, there is a hard gap at MY2010: the body-on-frame BL ended after MY2009 and the unibody XM arrived as a MY2011 built in West Point, Georgia. Sources conflict here because the XM launched globally in calendar 2009 as a '2010' model elsewhere; for the US market there is no 2010 Sorento, and Cars.com states this explicitly. That gap coincides with the most consequential engineering change on the nameplate — truck to crossover — so the boundary must not be smoothed. The Theta II GDI bearing failure spans the XM and UM generations, so the failure-mode hub for it needs to cross-link both pages.

known_issues.description: Front lower ball joint and control arm wear on the body-on-frame chassis.
Automatic transmission failures, particularly on the early 4-speed cars.

Theta II GDI connecting rod bearing failure from crankshaft machining debris restricting oil flow to the rod bearings; presents as knocking, power loss, then seizure or stall, occasionally with a punctured block and oil fire. Recall 17V-224 covered Theta II GDI Sorentos in this generation, and the later Knock Sensor Detection System software campaign added early-warning limp mode.
Electric power steering assist loss and column coupler complaints.

Theta II GDI connecting rod bearing failure continues; addressed through Kia's extended engine warranty and the Knock Sensor Detection System software campaign rather than a fresh mechanical recall for all years.
Engine compartment fire reports associated with oil leakage onto hot components following bearing failure; subject of NHTSA scrutiny across the Hyundai-Kia GDI fleet.
Tow hitch wiring harness can allow moisture ingress and short, causing a fire with the vehicle parked and off; subject to recall with an interim park-outside advisory, shared with the Telluride.
8-speed wet dual-clutch behind the 2.5T: low-speed shudder and hesitation from a stop.

notes: Clean four-generation map with no gaps; US first model year is 2001 (on sale January 2001 after an April 2000 New York show debut), matching the NHTSA span exactly. The Highlander Hybrid is not a separate NHTSA nameplate and sits inside each generation from MY2006 onward — worth flagging on each page because its failure profile (eCVT, HV battery, inverter) barely overlaps the conventional car's. The most useful engine boundary for a reliability site is inside gen 1, not at a generation edge: the 1MZ-FE V6 (2001-2003) carries the oil gelling history while the 3MZ-FE (2004-2007) does not.

known_issues.description: 1MZ-FE V6 oil gelling/sludge: the crankcase ventilation and oil return design allowed sludge to form and block oil passages, causing bearing and camshaft damage. Toyota ran an Oil Gel Customer Support Program covering the affected engine family.
2AZ-FE four-cylinder excessive oil consumption from piston ring design, and stripped cylinder head bolt threads in the aluminium block causing head gasket failure.

2GR-FE VVT-i oil supply line rupture: the rubber section of the variable valve timing oil hose can burst, dumping oil rapidly and causing engine damage. Recall covered 2GR-FE vehicles from roughly MY2007-2011, replacing the hose with an all-metal line.
Power window master switch overheating, a multi-model Toyota recall.
Denso low-pressure fuel pump impeller can deform and bind, stopping the pump and stalling the engine. Very large multi-brand recall.

build_notes: n/a: This generation has an unusually thin systemic-defect record; the fuel pump campaign is the dominant safety item. Useful as a baseline comparison generation on the site.

known_issues.description: Denso low-pressure fuel pump recall extends into the early years of this generation.

The 2023 switch from the long-serving 2GR-FKS V6 to the T24A-FTS turbo four is a major mid-generation powertrain change; the turbo four has no established long-term failure record yet and should be tracked separately from the V6 years on the page.

notes: Three generations, no gaps, and the NHTSA span (2010-2025) matches the US launch year exactly. The important structural fact for this nameplate is that its defining failure mode does NOT respect the generation boundary: recall 19V-120 covers 2012-2016 Souls with the 1.6L Gamma GDI engine, which straddles the AM (2012-2013) and PS (2014-2016) generations. The failure-mode hub page must cross-link both. Also note the Soul EV (US MY2015-2020) is built on the PS body and may share the 'SOUL' model name in the data — a BEV with no engine has an incompatible failure profile and should be separated if a fuel-type discriminator exists. The US Soul EV was discontinued after MY2020; the SK3-generation Soul EV was not sold in the US.

known_issues.description: 1.6L Gamma GDI: high exhaust gas temperatures overheat the catalytic converter, causing abnormal combustion that damages pistons and can break a connecting rod, puncturing the block. The escaping oil onto hot exhaust creates a fire risk. Recall 19V-120 (February 2019, ~379,000 vehicles) reflashed the catalytic overheating protection ECU logic and replaced damaged converters and engines.
Electric power steering assist loss complaints across the generation.
Trims without an engine immobilizer are easily stolen, driving a large theft loss pattern.

engines: 1.6L Gamma II T-GDI turbo I4 (Soul Turbo, 2017-2019)

known_issues.description: Same catalytic converter overheating and consequent piston/connecting rod failure as the previous generation, on the carryover 1.6L Gamma GDI. Recall 19V-120 covers MY2014-2016 cars alongside the MY2012-2013 AM cars.
Steering gear assembly fault allowing the steering wheel to separate from the column; subject to recall.

engines: 1.6L Gamma II T-GDI turbo I4 (GT-Line Turbo, 2020-2022)

known_issues.description: IVT (chain-type CVT) behaviour complaints — droning, hesitation and shudder — replacing the previous conventional automatic.
Early cars lacking an engine immobilizer are highly theft-prone; Kia made immobilizers standard partway through the generation and issued a software countermeasure for earlier units.

notes: This is the messiest nameplate in the assigned set, and the US split genuinely differs from Europe. Three specific hazards. (1) Mid-year changeovers: the Mk4 arrived mid-MY1999 as a '1999.5' alongside the outgoing Mk3, and the Mk5 arrived mid-MY2005 as a '2005.5' alongside the outgoing Mk4. MY1999 and MY2005 NHTSA records therefore contain two different cars each; I have assigned each boundary year to the incoming generation, but the pages must carry a disambiguation note. (2) Body-style desync: the Jetta SportWagen sold for MY2011-2014 was still the Mk5 PQ35 car even though the sedan had moved to the Mk6 for MY2011, so MY2011-2014 'JETTA' records mix two platforms depending on body style. The Mk4 wagon likewise continued into MY2006 alongside the Mk5 sedan. (3) The US Mk6 is a US-specific vehicle — a decontented 'New Compact Sedan' with a torsion-beam rear axle on base trims and cheaper interior materials — and is not the same car as the European Jetta of those years. Use the US split throughout.

known_issues.description: Window regulator failures — clips and cables break, dropping the glass into the door.
Coolant temperature sensor and ignition component failures causing stalling and no-start.

build_notes: n/a: MY1999 contains both this generation and the incoming Mk4, which arrived mid-year as a '1999.5'.

Ignition coil pack failures causing misfire and stalling; a large field campaign covered the affected coils.

known_issues.description: 2.0T FSI camshaft follower wear: the follower between the intake camshaft and the high-pressure fuel pump wears through, then the cam lobe itself, contaminating the engine with metal.
Timing chain tensioner failure on the later TSI, allowing the chain to jump and cause valve-to-piston contact.
2.0L TDI Common Rail high-pressure fuel pump failure sending metal debris through the entire fuel system, requiring full fuel system replacement.
DSG mechatronic unit failures producing sudden loss of drive; subject to campaign action.

generations.mixed_year_note: Both the outgoing and incoming generation were sold in this model year; NHTSA records do not separate them.
build_notes: n/a: The Jetta SportWagen stayed on this platform for MY2011-2014 after the sedan moved to the Mk6, so those SportWagen records belong here rather than with the Mk6 sedan.

known_issues.description: 2.0L TDI defeat device: engine control software detected emissions testing and reduced NOx output only during the test. EPA and CARB notices led to a buyback and modification program covering EA189 TDI vehicles.
Common Rail TDI high-pressure fuel pump failure contaminating the fuel system with metal.
EA888 Gen3 1.8T water pump and thermostat housing failures (plastic housing cracks and leaks).

build_notes: n/a: US-market-specific vehicle: decontented relative to the European Jetta of the same years, with a torsion-beam rear axle on base trims through MY2014. European reliability data for this generation does not transfer.

known_issues.description: No large systemic failure pattern established. Scattered turbocharger and water pump complaints on the 1.4/1.5 TSI.
8-speed automatic hesitation and rough low-speed shifting complaints.

notes: NHTSA's '3 SERIES' lumps sedan, wagon, coupe, convertible and M3 into one nameplate, and BMW ran body styles on offset model-year schedules, so a strict non-overlapping map requires choosing one body style as the spine. I have used the SEDAN, per the mainstream-passenger-version rule. The offsets to document on each page: the E36 coupe/convertible continued through MY1999 after the E46 sedan arrived; the E46 coupe/convertible ran MY2000-2006, so a MY2006 coupe is an E46 while a MY2006 sedan is an E90; the E92 coupe and E93 convertible ran MY2007-2013, so MY2012-2013 coupes are E9x while MY2012-2013 sedans are F30. From MY2014 the coupe and convertible left the nameplate entirely to become the 4 Series, which removes the ambiguity from that point forward. Verified US sedan first model years: E46 = 1999, E90 = 2006, F30 = 2012, G20 = 2019.

known_issues.description: Plastic cooling components fail with age: radiator end tanks, expansion tank, thermostat housing and the plastic water pump impeller. Failure typically ends in overheating and head gasket or head damage.
Rear subframe mounting point cracking in the chassis floor — the precursor to the better-known E46 version of the same defect.
Single-VANOS unit rattle and seal failure on M50TU/M52 engines.

build_notes: n/a: E36 coupes and convertibles continued through MY1999 after the E46 sedan arrived; MY1999 coupe/convertible records belong here.

known_issues.description: Rear subframe mounting point cracking: the trunk floor tears around the points where the rear subframe bolts to the body, because the spot welds and sheet metal are inadequate for the loads. Widespread across MY1999-2006 sedans and coupes; a US class action was filed in 2006 and settled in 2009. BMW's official remedy injected structural foam, which stiffened the area without addressing the weak spot welds, so recurrence is common.
Plastic thermostat housing, expansion tank and water pump failures causing overheating.
M54 oil filter housing gasket and valve cover gasket leaks — oil onto the belt and exhaust.
DISA intake manifold flap valve pivot failure, which can send debris into the engine.
S54 connecting rod bearing wear (M3 only), subject to a BMW rod bearing replacement campaign.

N54 high-pressure fuel pump failure causing extended cranking, stalling, and limp mode. BMW recalled roughly 130,000 N54-equipped US vehicles from MY2007-2010 and extended HPFP warranty coverage to 10 years / 120,000 miles.
N54 wastegate rattle from bushing wear, and direct injection index-12 injector failures.
Electric water pump and thermostat failure on N51/N52 engines, typically without warning.
Oil filter housing gasket and valve cover gasket leaks; VANOS solenoid faults on N52.

build_notes: n/a: E92 coupes and E93 convertibles continued through MY2013 after the F30 sedan arrived; MY2012-2013 coupe/convertible records belong here.

known_issues.description: N20/N26 timing chain and chain guide failure: the plastic guides are made from a material that embrittles and disintegrates, the chain then stretches or jumps, and the engine is commonly destroyed. Failures cluster around 50,000-80,000 miles. BMW of North America extended timing chain module warranty coverage to 7 years / 70,000 miles and a US class action settlement covered MY2012-2015 vehicles.
N20 oil filter housing gasket and valve cover gasket oil leaks.
N55 valve stem seal failure producing heavy blue smoke on startup.

build_notes: n/a: Coupes and convertibles left this nameplate for MY2014 to become the 4 Series; from MY2014 on, '3 SERIES' means sedan, wagon or Gran Turismo only. The F31 wagon and F34 Gran Turismo continued through MY2019, one year past the sedan.

build_notes: n/a: No systemic mechanical defect pattern is well documented for this generation yet; the B48/B58 engines resolved the N20 timing chain design. Complaint volume skews toward electronics and driver-assistance behaviour rather than powertrain. An LCI facelift arrived for MY2023 without a platform change.

notes: CRITICAL US-vs-Europe divergence. Europe got an all-new C1-platform Focus (Mk2) for 2005; North America did NOT. Ford instead re-skinned the original C170 car and sold it as the '2008-2011 Focus (second generation, North America)' - sedan and coupe only, no hatchback or wagon, same C170 unibody underneath. So the US has THREE Focus generations in this span while Europe has four, and the US 2008-2011 car is mechanically a facelifted 2000-2007 car. Grouping US 2008-2011 complaints with European Mk2 data would be wrong. NHTSA shows a 1999 model year, but the US Focus launched in autumn 1999 as a MY2000 vehicle - 1999-keyed records are almost certainly data-entry errors or early-build cars and should be folded into the 2000-2007 generation. US Focus ended with MY2018 (last car built 4 May 2018 at Michigan Assembly); the Mk4/C2 Focus Active was cancelled for the US, so there is no 2019+ US Focus. Naming caution: enthusiasts call the 2012-2018 car 'Mk3', which matches the global count, but US sources sometimes call it 'third generation' and sometimes 'Mk3.5' post-2015 facelift.

known_issues.description: The MY2000 Focus was one of the most-recalled vehicles of its era, with roughly a dozen NHTSA recall campaigns in its first two years covering front suspension, wheels, fuel system and electrical items. Early-build cars carry disproportionate complaint density and should be expected to skew the generation's totals.
Rear wheel bearing and rear spindle attachment failures, producing noise, play and in NHTSA recall cases the risk of wheel separation.
Coil pack failure on the 2.0L Zetec/Duratec causing misfire, rough running and stalling; a routine high-mileage failure item on this generation.
4F27E 4-speed automatic failures - harsh or slipping shifts and internal component wear, typically at higher mileage.

Carries over the C170 unibody, suspension and 4-speed automatic from the 2000-2007 car despite all-new sheet metal, so mechanical failure patterns closely track the prior generation rather than the European Mk2.
First-generation Ford SYNC debuted on the 2008 Focus; software freezes, Bluetooth pairing loss and audio dropouts are a recurring complaint category for these years.
4F27E 4-speed automatic - harsh engagement and internal failure at higher mileage, carried over unchanged from the first generation.

2.3L EcoBoost turbo I4 (350 hp), Focus RS 2016-2018

known_issues.description: Dry dual-clutch transmission shudder, slipping, hesitation on take-off, bucking and loss of motive power, caused by dry clutch friction material degradation and input shaft seal leakage contaminating the clutches. The Vargas v. Ford class action settlement covered 2012-2016 Focus (and 2011-2016 Fiesta), with buyback and cash remedies; later suits allege the defect persisted into 2017-2018 cars.
DPS6 transmission control module failure causing sudden loss of transmission engagement or unintended movement; subject of an NHTSA recall covering 2012-2016 Focus.
Door latch pawl spring tab can break, allowing a door to appear closed but open while driving; NHTSA recall covering 2012-2015 Focus.
Canister purge valve can stick open, drawing vacuum on the fuel tank, deforming it and causing stalling or no-start; recall and extended coverage issued.
Head gasket failure on Focus RS caused by use of a Mustang-specification cylinder head, allowing coolant loss and white exhaust smoke; Ford replaced heads and extended warranty coverage.

notes: There is NO 1996 US model year Wrangler. YJ production ended with MY1995; the TJ launched in spring 1996 as a MY1997 vehicle. NHTSA records keyed to 1996 are data errors (most likely 1995 YJ or 1997 TJ) and must not create a 1996 page. Two other overlaps matter: (a) the TJ Unlimited 'LJ' (2004-2006) is a long-wheelbase TJ, not a separate generation, but it is mechanically distinct enough to note; (b) MY2018 was sold as BOTH 'Wrangler JK' and the all-new 'Wrangler JL' concurrently - NHTSA 2018 records span two genuinely different vehicles and cannot be separated by model year alone. Use VIN or body-style hints if available; otherwise flag 2018 as mixed. The JK also introduced the first 4-door Wrangler (Unlimited, 2007+), which changes the vehicle's use profile substantially.

known_issues.description: Severe frame rail and body tub corrosion in road-salt regions, particularly at the rear frame section and skid plate mounts.
Peugeot BA-10/5 5-speed manual has a well-documented reputation for bearing and synchro failure under 4.2L/4.0L torque; replaced by the AX-15 for 1989.

Cylinder head casting number 0331 is prone to cracking between the number 3 exhaust valve seat and the coolant jacket, causing coolant loss into the cylinder, misfire and overheating. The 0331 casting was used across roughly the 2000-2004 build window.

'Death wobble' - violent self-sustaining oscillation of the solid front axle triggered at speed by a road input, driven by worn track bar bushings, ball joints, tie rod ends or steering damper on the coil-sprung solid-axle front end.
4.0L exhaust manifold cracking, typically at the rear runners, causing an exhaust leak and cold-start tick.
Corrosion of floor pans, rocker panels and frame rails in salt regions, commonly around the skid plate crossmember.

Left-bank (cylinders 1-3) cylinder head failure, typically a valve seat or valve guide defect producing a persistent tick, misfire and check-engine light. Chrysler issued an extended warranty on affected heads to 150,000 miles for early Pentastar builds.
Excessive oil consumption and piston/ring wear with associated cold-start tick on the 3.8L EGH V6; also weak on power relative to the vehicle's weight, especially in the 4-door Unlimited.
Totally Integrated Power Module failure causing no-start, fuel pump relay sticking on or off, stalling, and random accessory operation. A widely reported Chrysler-wide defect of this era.
'Death wobble' front-end oscillation from worn track bar, ball joints and steering linkage on the solid front axle; the subject of sustained NHTSA complaint volume across the generation.
Front axle inner 'C' and ball joint wear producing steering looseness and contributing to the wobble complaints, more pronounced on 4-door and larger-tire vehicles.

known_issues.description: 'Death wobble' returned on early JL vehicles; NHTSA opened investigation PE19-009 and FCA issued a revised steering damper and service actions. Complaint density is concentrated in the first two model years.
Clutch pressure plate can overheat and fracture, potentially breaching the bell housing and igniting nearby components; NHTSA recall covering manual-transmission 2018-2019 vehicles.
Defective high-voltage battery cells can cause thermal events and fire while parked; Stellantis recalled 4xe vehicles with a 'park outside and do not charge' advisory pending remedy.
Widespread reports of windshield cracking from minor impacts, attributed to the near-vertical windshield angle and glass specification.

notes: The US split is clean and matches the global generation count from the 6th generation onward, unlike the Accord (where the US got a wider body). Two caveats for data grouping: (1) Civic Hybrid, Civic Si, Civic Type R and the natural-gas Civic GX are sub-variants inside these generations with genuinely different failure modes - if NHTSA files them under 'CIVIC' they will contaminate the generation's profile (the IMA battery complaints in 2006-2011, for example, come only from the hybrid). (2) The 9th generation received an unusually early and extensive facelift for MY2013, one year after launch, in response to reviewer criticism - it is a facelift, not a new generation, but 2012 cars differ noticeably in interior materials and structure from 2013-2015. The 2014 model year also swapped the 5-speed automatic for a CVT on the 1.8L, a mid-generation powertrain change that matters for failure patterns.

known_issues.description: 4-speed automatic failure - slipping, flaring between gears and outright loss of drive, a recurring pattern across late-1990s Honda automatics.
Distributor internal failure (ignition coil and igniter module inside the distributor housing) causing intermittent no-start, stalling and misfire.
Corrosion of rear wheel arches, rear subframe and strut mounts in road-salt regions.
Honda Multi Matic CVT belt and start-clutch failures on the HX trim; a low-volume variant with a high failure rate relative to the conventional automatic.

Automatic transmission failure - torque converter lock-up clutch judder progressing to slipping and complete loss of drive. Honda extended the automatic transmission warranty on affected 2001-2002 Civics to 7 years / 100,000 miles.

Takata ammonium-nitrate inflators on 2001-2003 Civics are among the highest-risk 'Alpha' population, with a documented rupture rate high enough that NHTSA and Honda issued do-not-drive advisories. Inflator rupture propels metal fragments into the cabin.
Front and rear engine mount collapse causing vibration at idle and driveline clunk; a routine failure item on this generation.

Cylinder block casting flaw on the 1.8L R18 allows the block to crack and seep coolant, leading to overheating, warped cylinder head and eventual engine failure. Honda extended engine block warranty coverage to 10 years from purchase with no mileage limit and replaces the block or full engine at no charge.

Integrated Motor Assist battery pack degradation causing sharply reduced assist and fuel economy. Honda's remedial software update reduced electric assist to protect the pack, which prompted a class action settlement over the resulting performance and economy loss.
Takata inflator recall population; rupture risk on driver and passenger inflators.
A/C condenser and compressor failure, with compressor debris contaminating the system and requiring full-system replacement.
Sun visor hinge failure causing the visor to droop; Honda issued a warranty extension for replacement.

Start-clutch judder and shudder on light acceleration after the 2014 switch from the 5-speed automatic to a CVT on the 1.8L; addressed by control software updates and fluid service. Note this defect cannot exist on 2012-2013 cars, which used a conventional automatic.
A/C condenser refrigerant leaks causing loss of cooling; a high-volume complaint across the generation.
Takata inflator recall population continues through this generation.
IMA battery degradation on the Civic Hybrid, same failure mechanism as the prior generation.

A/C condenser leaks causing loss of cooling; subject of extended warranty coverage and litigation.

Control software fault could cause the engine to stall while driving; addressed by a Toyota recall covering the US-market 2001-2003 cars.
Combination meter failure producing a blank or partially blank display, requiring cluster replacement.

engines: 1.5L 1NZ-FXE Atkinson-cycle I4 with THS II (76 hp engine, 110 hp combined)

known_issues.description: Inverter IGBT and IPM failure causing sudden loss of hybrid power and the 'red triangle of death' warning, sometimes at speed. Toyota issued inverter software recalls and extended warranty coverage on the inverter assembly.
Combination meter self-illumination failure leaving the speedometer and fuel display blank; subject of a Toyota warranty enhancement program.
Steering intermediate extension shaft can crack and separate, causing loss of steering control; NHTSA recall.
Traction battery cooling fan and duct clogging with debris causes the pack to overheat and accelerates cell degradation - a maintenance-driven failure specific to this packaging.
Electric engine coolant pump failure causing overheating warnings; a recurring high-mileage failure item.

engines: 1.8L 2ZR-FXE Atkinson-cycle I4 (98 hp engine, 134 hp combined)

known_issues.description: The EGR cooler and intake-side EGR passages accumulate heavy carbon deposits, restricting flow and driving localized combustion heat that fails the head gasket between cylinders. Symptoms are cold-start misfire (P0300/P0301), coolant loss with no external leak, and rhythmic shake on startup. The EGR cooler itself can also leak coolant internally, producing near-identical symptoms at far lower repair cost. This is the defining failure mode of the generation.
Excessive oil consumption on the 2ZR-FXE traced to piston ring design, commonly one quart per 1,000-2,000 miles, which accelerates the EGR carbon fouling above.

ABS and regenerative braking handoff software could produce a momentary loss of braking response over bumpy or slick surfaces; the subject of Toyota's February 2010 recall, one of the highest-profile Prius actions.
Inverter IGBT control software could allow the hybrid system to shut down while driving; covered by a 2014 Toyota recall spanning the generation.
Electric coolant pump failure causing overheating and hybrid system warnings.

known_issues.description: Engine-compartment wire harness connected to the hybrid power control unit can chafe against the housing, wear through insulation and short, producing smoke or fire; large Toyota recall covering the early years of the generation.
Parking brake cable can fail to engage properly, allowing the vehicle to roll away when parked without the transmission in Park; NHTSA recall.
Inverter and hybrid system control software fault could cause the hybrid system to shut down and the vehicle to lose power while driving; recall issued.

engines: 2.0L M20A-FXS Atkinson-cycle I4 (194 hp FWD / 196 hp AWD combined)
2.0L M20A-FXS plug-in hybrid (220 hp combined), Prius Prime 2023-2024 / Prius Plug-in Hybrid 2025+

notes: Three structural reversals make this nameplate unusually treacherous: unibody (R50) to body-on-frame (R51) to unibody again (R52). A 2004 Pathfinder and a 2005 Pathfinder are completely different vehicles with different frames, engines and transmissions - the 2004/2005 boundary is the most important in the list. THERE IS NO 2021 US MODEL YEAR: Nissan skipped MY2021 entirely between the R52 and R53. Any 2021-keyed record is a data error. The R52-to-R53 break also swapped the JATCO Xtronic CVT for a ZF 9-speed conventional automatic, which is the single biggest reliability-relevant change in the model's history and must not be smeared across the boundary. First-generation WD21 (1987-1995) falls outside the NHTSA span but is listed for completeness.

known_issues.description: Structural corrosion of the frame and rear body sections in salt regions; the dominant end-of-life failure for this generation.
Exhaust manifold cracking on the VG33E producing a cold-start tick and exhaust leak.
Corrosion of the rear strut towers, rocker panels and rear frame rails in road-salt regions - a significant safety concern on a unibody vehicle.

known_issues.description: The internal transmission fluid cooler inside the radiator can fail, allowing engine coolant to mix with automatic transmission fluid. The resulting emulsion (widely called the 'strawberry milkshake of death') destroys the transmission. Subject of a class action settlement and Nissan warranty extension covering the affected Pathfinder/Xterra/Frontier population.
VQ40DE timing chain guide and tensioner wear producing a cold-start rattle and, if ignored, chain skip.
Exhaust manifold and catalytic converter failure on the VQ40DE.

transmissions: JATCO CVT8 / CVT8HT Xtronic continuously variable

known_issues.description: CVT belt slip condition producing shudder, judder, hesitation, overheating and sudden loss of motive power. This is the generation's defining failure mode and drives most of its complaint volume.
Secondary hood latch can corrode and fail to hold, allowing the hood to fly open while driving; NHTSA recall.
Brake fluid can leak from the ABS actuator pump onto the circuit board, creating a short and fire risk; recall issued for affected Nissan models including the Pathfinder.

build_notes: Powertrain (mid-generation change): The MY2017 facelift replaced the port-injected VQ35DE with the direct-injection VQ35DD. Direct injection introduces intake valve carbon deposit exposure absent from 2013-2016 cars.

known_issues.description: The JATCO CVT was replaced by a ZF 9-speed conventional automatic for this generation. Too recent for established systemic failure patterns; a MY2025 facelift refreshed styling and trim.

notes: THE MOST DANGEROUS NAMEPLATE IN THIS BATCH. 'TrailBlazer' covers two entirely unrelated vehicles separated by an 11-year gap: a 4,500 lb body-on-frame midsize truck-based SUV with an inline-six or V8 (2002-2009), and a 3,200 lb front-drive subcompact crossover with a 1.2L or 1.3L three-cylinder (2021-present). Merging them would be the worst possible outcome for this site. Note the capitalisation shift Chevrolet itself used: 'TrailBlazer' for the SUV, 'Trailblazer' for the crossover. Three further caveats: (1) 'TrailBlazer' was also an appearance package on the S-10 Blazer for roughly 1999-2002 - those complaints belong under BLAZER, not here; (2) NHTSA may file 'TRAILBLAZER EXT' (2002-2006 long wheelbase) separately, and the TrailBlazer SS (2006-2009, 6.0L LS2) is a different mechanical animal inside the GMT360 generation; (3) the 2012-2020 global Trailblazer (Thailand/Brazil-built body-on-frame, Colorado-based) was NEVER sold in the US or Canada, so no US complaints should exist for those years.

known_issues.description: Blower motor resistor overheats and fails because of an inadequate cooling design, leaving the fan operating only on the highest speed setting. One of the highest-frequency complaints on the platform across all years.

Stepper motors behind the gauges fail, causing the speedometer, tachometer, fuel and temperature gauges to read inaccurately or stop entirely. GM issued special coverage for affected clusters and a repair/reman industry exists specifically for this failure.

Fuel level sender inside the fuel pump module fails, producing an erratic gauge that sticks on empty or reads wildly wrong; remedy requires replacing the complete fuel pump module assembly. GM agreed to cover 50 percent of repair cost on 2005-2007 vehicles even though the failure spans 2002-2008.
Exhaust valve seat recession and valve damage on early Atlas inline-sixes, producing misfire, low compression on affected cylinders and rough running.
Transfer case encoder motor and selector switch failure producing a 'Service 4WD' warning and inability to shift between 2WD and 4WD ranges.
Front wheel bearing hub assembly and ball joint wear producing ABS faults, noise and steering play; a routine high-mileage failure item on GMT360.

engines: 1.3L L3T turbocharged I3 (155 hp), FWD and AWD

known_issues.description: Completely unrelated to the 2002-2009 GMT360 TrailBlazer - front-wheel-drive unibody subcompact crossover with a three-cylinder turbo engine, sharing its platform with the Buick Encore GX and Chevrolet Trax. None of the GMT360 failure modes apply.

Complaint volume centres on the CVT used with front-wheel drive - hesitation, drone and shudder reports - while AWD models use a conventional 9-speed automatic. Drivetrain choice determines the transmission entirely, so 2021-2025 records should be segmented by FWD/AWD where possible.
Too recent for established long-term failure patterns. A MY2024 facelift updated the exterior, infotainment and interior.
