Panoramic moonroof glass shattering and water intrusion complaints.

notes: Contiguous, no gaps, 1997 through present. Two boundaries deserve care. (1) The 2007-2017 third generation is unusually long — eleven model years — and contains a hard powertrain break: 5.4L Triton V8 through MY2014, 3.5L EcoBoost V6 from MY2015 with the 2015 facelift. For failure-mode analysis 2007-2014 and 2015-2017 behave like two different vehicles even though the platform (U324/U354) is one generation. (2) Sources disagree on whether the 2025 car is a true fifth generation or a very heavy redesign of the U553: Wikipedia and Ford's own marketing treat it as a new generation, but the T3 frame architecture and 3.5L EcoBoost/10R80 powertrain carry over. I have listed it as a separate generation because body, interior, electrical architecture and trim structure all changed, which is what matters for complaint grouping. Extended-length variants (Expedition EL 2007-2017, Expedition MAX 2018-2024) share the generation and its defects. Lincoln Navigator is the corporate twin throughout.

known_issues.description: Two-valve Triton spark plug ejection. The aluminum cylinder head carries only about four threads of engagement; plugs work loose under cylinder pressure and blow out, stripping the head threads and requiring insert repair or head replacement.

Texas Instruments speed control deactivation switch mounted on the master cylinder leaks brake fluid onto energized contacts, overheats and ignites — fires occur with the engine off and key out. Covered by Ford's large speed-control switch recall campaigns (05V-388 and successors).
Rear air suspension air spring and compressor leaks causing rear-end sag and compressor burnout.

Three-valve 5.4L two-piece spark plug design: the lower ground-shield section seizes in the head from carbon buildup and snaps off during removal, requiring specialized extraction and often head damage.

Variable cam timing phaser rattle. Oil-fed cam phasers lose control authority when hot idle oil pressure or oil condition degrades, producing a diesel-like rattle at cold start and idle, and can progress to timing chain and cam damage.
Rear air suspension air spring and compressor failure (independent rear suspension introduced this generation).

5.4L 3V cam phaser rattle and timing chain/tensioner wear — oil starvation to the top end at cold start wears the phasers, producing the characteristic rattle; replacement often does not hold and the common field fix is locking out the variable cam timing.
5.4L 3V two-piece spark plugs seizing and breaking off in the cylinder head during service.
3.5L EcoBoost timing chain stretch and cam phaser wear, plus turbocharger and intercooler condensation-related misfires under sustained load.
Rear load-leveling air suspension compressor and air spring failure.

engines: 3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 (375 hp / 400 hp Platinum; 440 hp Timberline and later)

known_issues.description: 10R80 10-speed automatic harsh and erratic shifting, clunk on the 4-5 and 6-7 changes, and torque converter lockup shudder. Addressed through repeated PCM/TCM recalibrations rather than hardware.

Under-hood fires traced to the engine compartment on 3.5L EcoBoost Expedition and Navigator, prompting a Ford recall with an interim advice to park outdoors and a revised under-hood harness/battery routing remedy.
Battery drain and stop/start system faults on early build years.

generations.platform_code: U724 / U725 (Ford T3 frame, carried over from U553)
engines: 3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 (400 hp / 480 lb-ft — Active, King Ranch, Platinum)
3.5L EcoBoost twin-turbo V6 (440 hp / 510 lb-ft — Tremor)

known_issues.description: Too new for an established systemic defect pattern; complaint volume is dominated by first-year build and infotainment/electrical items rather than confirmed mechanical failure modes.

notes: Contiguous, no gaps. All generations are US-market vehicles designed primarily for North America, so no US-vs-global split issue. Two mid-generation powertrain changes matter more than the facelifts: (1) MY2006 added Variable Cylinder Management to FWD first-generation Pilots, and (2) within the third generation the transmission is split by trim — 6-speed automatic on lower trims and ZF 9-speed on Touring/Elite for 2016-2020, with the 9-speed becoming standard across all trims for 2021-2022. That trim split means MY2016-2020 complaint records must be separated by transmission, not just by year. The fourth generation dropped cylinder deactivation entirely.

generations.platform_code: YF1 / YF2 (Honda Global Midsize, shared with Odyssey RL3 and Acura MDX YD1)
engines: 3.5L J35A4 / J35A6 SOHC VTEC V6 (240-244 hp)
3.5L J35A9 V6 with Variable Cylinder Management (FWD, 2006-2008)

known_issues.description: Honda 5-speed automatic torque converter lockup clutch judder and third-gear clutch failure — the same defect family that drove Honda's V6 automatic warranty extensions of that era. Symptoms are shudder at light throttle around 40-50 mph followed by slipping and failure.
J35 timing belt is a scheduled-replacement item (not a chain); belt or tensioner neglect on this interference engine causes catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.
Power steering pump and high-pressure hose leaks producing whine and fluid loss.

engines: 3.5L J35Z4 SOHC VTEC V6 (250 hp) with Variable Cylinder Management

known_issues.description: Variable Cylinder Management-related excessive oil consumption and spark plug fouling. Running on three cylinders wears the piston rings on the deactivated bank, oil enters the combustion chamber, plugs foul and misfire codes set. Honda issued warranty extensions covering spark plug fouling and piston-ring wear on VCM-equipped J35 engines and settled related class litigation.
Active/hydraulic engine mount failure producing heavy vibration in VCM three-cylinder mode.

engines: 3.5L J35Y6 direct-injected SOHC V6 (280 hp) with Variable Cylinder Management and idle stop
transmissions: ZF 9HP48 9-speed automatic (Touring/Elite 2016-2020; standard on all trims 2021-2022)

known_issues.description: ZF 9-speed (9HP48) low-speed jerkiness, hesitation from a stop, harsh 1-2 and 2-3 engagement and erratic gear selection with the electronic push-button shifter. Honda addressed it with successive TCM software recalibrations rather than hardware; early build years are the worst. Only Touring and Elite trims carried the 9-speed until 2021.
Direct-injection fuel injector failure and carbon buildup on intake valves; VCM-related oil dilution and consumption complaints continue from the previous generation.
Idle-stop (auto start-stop) restart faults and infotainment/head-unit freezing and reboot complaints.

engines: 3.5L J35Y8 V6 (285 hp) — cylinder deactivation (VCM) deleted

known_issues.description: Too new for an established systemic defect pattern. Early complaint clusters concern 10-speed shift quality and infotainment/electrical behavior rather than confirmed mechanical failure modes. Notably, dropping VCM removes the oil-consumption mechanism that defined the two prior generations.

notes: Single generation only — the Cobalt existed for exactly six model years, 2005 through 2010, and the NHTSA span matches it exactly. It replaced the Cavalier and was replaced by the Cruze for MY2011. There is no second generation and no gap. The unrelated Chevrolet Cobalt sold in Latin America and Russia from 2011 is a different vehicle (Gamma II sedan) and does not appear in US NHTSA data. Platform twins whose complaint patterns mirror the Cobalt's: Pontiac G5/Pursuit, Pontiac G4, Saturn Ion (Delta), HHR (ignition switch and EPS recalls overlap). This nameplate has an extraordinarily high complaint-per-vehicle rate because of the ignition switch scandal, so raw complaint counts for 2005-2010 are inflated by recall publicity — worth flagging on the page.

engines: 2.0L Ecotec LSJ supercharged I4 (205 hp, SS, 2005-2007)
2.0L Ecotec LNF turbocharged I4 (260 hp, SS, 2008-2010)

known_issues.description: The ignition switch detent plunger and spring provide insufficient torque to hold the key in RUN. Knee contact with the key ring, a heavy key fob, or a rough road can rotate the key to ACCESSORY or OFF, shutting off the engine and with it power steering and power brake assist, and — critically — disabling the airbag system so it will not deploy in the ensuing crash. GM recall 14V-047 (February 2014) covered 2005-2010 Cobalt; NHTSA fined GM $35 million for concealing the defect for roughly a decade. Thirteen deaths were initially acknowledged; the victim compensation fund ultimately recognized 124.

Electric power steering (EPS) motor and torque sensor failure causing sudden total loss of steering assist at any speed, with steering effort spiking without warning. NHTSA recall 10V-073 (2010), expanded under 14V-153, covering roughly 1.3 million Cobalt and Pontiac G5 vehicles.

Ecotec timing chain stretch on the 2.2L and 2.4L, announced by a cold-start rattle and setting cam/crank correlation codes; often driven by excessive oil consumption and PCV-system oil carryover that lets the chain run dry.

notes: Contiguous, no gaps. US model-year boundaries: 1995-2004, 2005-2015, 2016-2023, 2024-present. The one commonly misremembered boundary is the third-to-fourth: the fourth-generation N400 started production in December 2023 but is a MY2024 vehicle, so MY2023 is the last third-generation year — several sources loosely say '2023' for the new truck because of the reveal date. Note also that the second generation is unusually long (eleven model years) with a substantial 2012 facelift that is not a new generation. The Tacoma's dominant historical failure mode is not powertrain but structural: frame corrosion, addressed through two separate Toyota programs covering 1995-2004 and 2005-2010.

known_issues.description: Frame rail rust-through and perforation from inadequate rustproofing, severe enough that frames could separate. Toyota created a 15-year unlimited-mileage corrosion warranty covering more than 800,000 trucks, with frame replacement or vehicle buyback; coverage originally announced for 1995-2000 and later extended to 2001-2004.
Front lower ball joint wear leading to separation and loss of steering control — the subject of Toyota ball-joint recall activity spanning the late first generation into the early second generation.

generations.platform_code: N220-N270 (shares architecture with 4Runner N210/N280 and FJ Cruiser)

known_issues.description: Frame corrosion again. A November 2016 class settlement required Toyota to inspect and, where necessary, replace rusted frames on 2005-2010 model year Tacomas, with a 12-year inspection program.
Rear leaf spring leaf fracture; a broken leaf can move rearward and puncture the fuel tank, creating a fire and loss-of-control risk. Toyota recall coverage on 2005-2010 trucks.
Front lower ball joint separation recall covering the early second generation.
Steering intermediate shaft and rack clunk/looseness, a very high-frequency complaint across the generation.

engines: 3.5L 2GR-FKS V6 (278 hp), D-4S port + direct injection, Atkinson-cycle operation at cruise

known_issues.description: Six-speed automatic gear hunting, harsh and delayed downshifts, and torque converter lockup shudder — the single largest complaint cluster for this generation. Toyota issued multiple TSBs, four of them transmission-related, and repeated control-software reflashes. The Atkinson-cycle 2GR-FKS's narrow low-rpm torque band aggravates the hunting behavior.

Rear differential oil leak at the carrier-to-axle-housing joint from insufficiently torqued fastening nuts. Continued operation can damage or seize the differential and lock the rear wheels. Recall covered essentially all 2016-2017 Tacomas, roughly 228,000 US trucks; remedy is re-torque or nut and gasket replacement, with carrier assembly replacement where damaged.
Rear leaf spring and bed/frame corrosion complaints continue, though at lower rates than the prior generation.

engines: 2.4L i-FORCE MAX turbocharged hybrid I4 (326 hp)
transmissions: 6-speed manual (iMT, available on selected TRD trims)

known_issues.description: Too new for an established systemic defect pattern. First-generation-of-a-new-architecture caveats apply: entirely new turbocharged four-cylinder and hybrid powertrain, new 8-speed automatic and coil-spring rear suspension on some trims. Treat 2024-2025 complaint data as early-build noise until volume accumulates.

notes: CRITICAL DATA HAZARD — three carryover overlaps where two different trucks share one model year under one nameplate. (1) MY1999-2000: the outgoing GMT400 was sold alongside the new GMT800 as the 'Sierra Classic' (1500 Classic 1999 only, then 2500/3500 for 2000). (2) MY2007: the GMT800 continued as 'Sierra Classic' alongside the new GMT900. (3) MY2019: the K2XX continued as 'Sierra Limited' alongside the new T1XX. In each case NHTSA records for that model year can contain either truck, so any 1999, 2007 or 2019 grouping must be treated as mixed unless VIN-decoded. I have kept the generation list contiguous and non-overlapping (splitting at 1999, 2007, 2014, 2019) and flagged the carryovers here rather than creating overlapping ranges. The NHTSA 'SIERRA 1500' nameplate begins at MY1999; the 1996-1998 GMT400 trucks are usually filed under 'SIERRA' or 'C/K 1500' and I have listed that generation for completeness. Chevrolet Silverado 1500 is the mechanical twin throughout and shares every failure mode listed.

known_issues.description: Central port / spider injection (CSFI) poppet-nozzle leakage on Vortec V6 and V8 engines causing hard starting, rough running and raw fuel in the intake.
4L60-E 3-4 clutch pack burnout, the classic failure of this transmission family.
Instrument cluster stepper motor (gauge motor) failure causing erratic, sticking or dead speedometer, tachometer and fuel gauge. So widespread GM issued a warranty extension on the cluster.
4L60-E / 4L65-E 3-4 clutch pack failure producing slipping on the 3-4 shift and eventual loss of drive.
Fuel level sending unit failure from sulfur deposits on the sender card, giving false or stuck fuel readings.
Transfer case encoder motor failure on 4WD/AWD models causing shift-mode failure and stuck-in-neutral conditions.

engines: 5.3L Vortec LMG / LC9 / LH6 V8 with Active Fuel Management

known_issues.description: Active Fuel Management (AFM) excessive oil consumption on Gen IV 5.3L V8s. The AFM oil pressure relief valve in the crankcase sprays oil onto the cylinder walls while worn low-tension piston rings fail to control it; the result is oil burn of roughly a quart per 1,500-2,000 miles, fouled spark plugs on the deactivated cylinders, and collapsed AFM lifters that wipe camshaft lobes. Subject of the Sloan v. GM and Siqueiros v. GM class actions.
Brake and fuel line corrosion perforation on salt-belt trucks, a very high-frequency NHTSA complaint category for this generation.
6L80-E torque converter and valve body wear producing harsh shifts and shudder.

engines: 6.2L EcoTec3 L86 V8 (all direct-injected with Active Fuel Management)

known_issues.description: 8L90 eight-speed torque converter shudder. Dexron VI fluid degrades and loses friction stability, producing a chuggle or shudder at light throttle around 25-60 mph plus harsh 2-3 and 3-4 shifts and clunks. GM issued repeated TSBs, eventually moving to Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP; a class action over the 8-speed reached settlement in 2023.
AFM lifter collapse on L83 and L86 V8s. A deactivating lifter fails to re-extend, causing a dead cylinder, misfire codes and wiped camshaft lobes; usually accompanied by elevated oil consumption.
Excessive oil consumption on early direct-injected 5.3L trucks, tied to the AFM system and piston ring design.

engines: 5.3L L84 V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management
6.2L L87 V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management

known_issues.description: 6.2L L87 V8 connecting rod and crankshaft bearing failure. Manufacturing defects — sediment embedded on connecting rods and contamination in crankshaft oil galleries — overload the bearings, causing knock, seizure and in some cases a connecting rod breach through the block, with sudden loss of propulsion. GM recalled roughly 600,000 US vehicles in April 2025 covering 2021-2024 Sierra 1500, Silverado 1500, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and Escalade; NHTSA's investigation scoped as many as 877,710 vehicles. Remedy is inspection, then either engine replacement or an oil filter change plus a switch from 0W-20 to eight quarts of 0W-40 synthetic. MY2025 vehicles are excluded.
Dynamic Fuel Management (DFM) lifter failure on the 5.3L L84 and 6.2L L87, the successor mechanism to the earlier AFM lifter problem — collapsed lifter, dead cylinder, camshaft lobe damage.
10L80 ten-speed harsh shifting, clunk and torque converter shudder; 8L90 shudder complaints continue on 8-speed trucks.

notes: US-vs-global note: US model-year boundaries run one year behind the global launch years, which is the single most common source of error here. The BK launched globally in 2003 but is MY2004-2009 in the US; the BL launched in 2008 but is MY2010-2013 in the US; the BM launched in 2013 but is MY2014-2018 in the US; the BP is MY2019-present in both. Use the US boundaries. Contiguous, no gaps. The most important mid-generation change is inside the BL: for MY2012-2013 the US car switched to the SkyActiv-G 2.0 with SkyActiv-Drive 6-speed automatic or SkyActiv-MT 6-speed manual, replacing the MZR engines and 5-speed transmissions — the 2010-2011 and 2012-2013 BL cars have materially different powertrain failure profiles despite being one generation. Mazdaspeed3 (2007-2009 BK, 2010-2013 BL) is a high-output variant within its generation, not a separate one. The 'MAZDA3' nameplate replaced the Protegé; NHTSA data begins 2004 accordingly.

generations.platform_code: BK (Ford C1 / Mazda global C platform, shared with Ford Focus Mk2 and Volvo S40)
engines: 2.3L MZR DISI turbo I4 (263 hp, Mazdaspeed3 2007-2009)

known_issues.description: Rear wheel arch and rocker panel rust perforation on salt-belt cars, often visible before 8 years of age — the defining durability complaint for this generation.
Clock spring failure in the steering column causing airbag warning lights, inoperative horn and dead steering wheel controls.
Takata inflator recalls cover a large share of this generation.

engines: 2.3L MZR DISI turbo I4 (263 hp, Mazdaspeed3)

known_issues.description: Major mid-generation powertrain change: MY2012-2013 replaced the 2.0L MZR and its 5-speed transmissions with the SkyActiv-G 2.0 and SkyActiv 6-speed manual/automatic. Complaint patterns for 2010-2011 and 2012-2013 should not be pooled.
Clock spring and traction control module faults; door lock actuator failures.
Continued rear arch and subframe corrosion complaints in salt-belt states, though reduced versus the BK.

Mazda Connect TFT display delamination and ghost-touch behavior — the screen changes stations or navigation input on its own while the car is stationary. Replacement is expensive when not covered by goodwill.

Water entry into the rear brake caliper corrodes the electric parking brake actuator shaft, which can bind and leave the parking brake applied or inoperative. Recall covering certain 2014-2016 cars. Separately, premature rear brake pad and rotor wear is a high-frequency complaint.
Fuel tank shut-off valve can allow liquid fuel into the evaporative emissions system, creating a leak and fire risk. Recall covering certain 2015-2016 cars.

Incorrectly manufactured exhaust valve springs that may fracture in service, causing engine stall. Recall covering certain 2018 cars. Separately, front timing cover oil seepage and intake valve carbon deposits from direct injection with PCV oil carryover.

engines: 2.5L SkyActiv-G I4 (186 hp) with cylinder deactivation
2.5L SkyActiv-G Turbo I4 (227 hp on 87 octane / 250 hp on 93 octane, 2021+)

known_issues.description: Excessive oil consumption attributed to valve stem seals on certain turbocharged cars, the subject of a class-action settlement.

Automatic lighting system malfunction warnings, reported particularly under high ambient temperature; i-stop (idle stop) software fault where the engine may fail to restart after entering idle-stop mode, addressed by recall/software campaign.
Transmission control module faults producing drivetrain malfunction warnings and limp-home behavior.

notes: THE MOST US-vs-GLOBAL DIVERGENT MODEL IN THIS SET — two hard traps. (1) GAP: there was no MY2011 Passat in the United States. The B6 ended with MY2010 and the Chattanooga-built NMS began with MY2012. Europe received the B7 (a B6 facelift) for 2011-2014; the US never got it. Do not bridge 2010 to 2012. (2) The 2012-2022 US Passat ('NMS', New Midsize Sedan) is a North America-specific vehicle built in Chattanooga on a stretched PQ46-derived platform. It is NOT the European B7 or B8 Passat and shares almost nothing with them beyond the badge — merging US and European Passat data would be a serious error. (3) B5 vs B5.5: enthusiasts split these, but the mid-2000 B5.5 change was a facelift on the same longitudinal PL45 platform, so per the platform rule I have kept 1998-2005 as one generation and noted the split. Sources also disagree on the US B4 window; VW of America sold the B4 for MY1995-1997 with the B5 arriving for MY1998. Final US model year is 2022, closed out by a Limited Edition run of 1,973 cars.

known_issues.description: 01M four-speed automatic valve body and clutch pack failure, a chronic VW/Audi transverse automatic problem of this era.
Plastic coolant flange and thermostat housing cracking causing coolant loss and overheating.
Window regulator cable failure and wiring harness insulation degradation.

generations.platform_code: PL45 (VW B5, longitudinal engine, shared with Audi B5 A4)

known_issues.description: 1.8T oil sludge / oil gelling. Undersized oil drainback passages plus conventional oil and long intervals let sludge form, starving the turbo and bearings and destroying the engine. VW issued an extended warranty and settlement covering 1.8T engines from roughly 1997-2004.
Ignition coil pack failure causing sudden misfire and limp mode; multiple VW recall and extended-coverage campaigns.
Window regulator cable failure — the glass drops into the door. Extremely high-frequency complaint.
W8 timing chain and chain tensioner complexity with very high repair cost and low parts availability; four camshaft chains driven off the crank.

The mid-2000 B5.5 facelift (US MY2001.5 onward) brought a new dashboard, revised body panels and engine changes on the same PL45 platform. Enthusiast sources treat B5 and B5.5 as separate; the platform did not change, so it is one generation here.

generations.platform_code: PQ46 (transverse engine — a fundamental architecture change from the longitudinal B5)
engines: 2.0L FSI/TSI turbo I4 (BPY 200 hp, later CCTA 200 hp)

known_issues.description: High-pressure fuel pump cam follower wear-through. The bucket follower riding the intake camshaft lobe wears through, then the pump plunger machines the camshaft lobe, filling the engine with metal. Requires camshaft and often HPFP replacement; inspection interval became a de facto maintenance item.
Timing chain tensioner failure on the 2.0T allowing chain slack and valve-to-piston contact; carbon buildup on intake valves inherent to early direct injection without port injection.

Blocked sunroof drains flood the driver footwell and soak the comfort control module and other under-carpet electronics, producing seemingly random electrical faults. One of the most-reported B6 problems.
ABS control module failure causing ABS/ESP warning lights and loss of stability control.

2.0L TDI diesel defeat device. Engine control software detected emissions testing and reduced NOx output only during the test. US Passat TDI model years 2012-2015 were included in the Volkswagen emissions settlement with buyback or emissions modification; TDI sales were permanently discontinued after MY2015.
DQ250 DSG mechatronic unit faults on TDI cars causing harsh engagement, flare and limp mode.
ABS module and various body-control electrical faults; door wiring harness chafing.
Not a defect but essential for data hygiene: this vehicle is unrelated to the contemporaneous European B7/B8 Passat. US complaint data for 2012-2022 describes a distinct, simpler, US-only car.

notes: The 200 nameplate exists only for MY2011-2017. Gen 1 is not a clean-sheet car: it is a re-engineered/restyled Chrysler Sebring (JS, 2007-2010), so failure patterns carry over from the Sebring and its Dodge Avenger twin — complaint grouping should treat 2011-2014 200 and 2007-2010 Sebring as mechanically continuous even though the nameplate changed. Gen 1 offered sedan and convertible; gen 2 is sedan-only, so any convertible complaint in the data is necessarily gen 1. Gen 2 was killed after MY2017 when Sterling Heights was converted to Ram production; there is no 2018+ 200. The two generations share almost nothing (Mitsubishi-derived JS vs Fiat-derived CUSW), so a merged page would be badly misleading.

known_issues.description: Totally Integrated Power Module (TIPM) failure — internal relay/solder degradation, most commonly the fuel pump relay, causing no-start, stall while driving, and unrelated multi-system electrical faults (wipers, horn, lights). Shared with other 2011-2014 Chrysler/Dodge products using the 04692346-family TIPM.
Unexpected engine stalling without stored fault codes, concentrated in the early years of the generation; a large share of the generation's ODI complaint volume.
The 4-speed automatic paired with the 2.4L (base trims) draws harsh/erratic shift and durability complaints; the 6-speed 62TE is the stronger pairing.

2.4L Tigershark excessive oil consumption — piston ring / cylinder bore incompatibility allows oil past the rings to be burned; owners report roughly a quart per 1,000 miles, and the low-oil-pressure warning does not illuminate early enough to prevent running low, leading to unexpected shutdown. Subject of the Wood v. FCA US class action and FCA Customer Satisfaction Notifications; FCA also attributed part of the consumption to Interactive Deceleration Fuel ShutOff (IDFSO) calibration drawing oil into the cylinders on overrun.

ZF 948TE 9-speed harsh, erratic, and delayed shifting, hunting between gears, and unexpected shifts to neutral. FCA addressed it through repeated TSB software reflashes, which owners widely described as only marginally effective; the same transmission drew recalls in sister vehicles (Cherokee KL, Renegade).
Rotary electronic gear selector draws misapplied-gear and shift-confirmation complaints; unlike a conventional PRNDL it gives no mechanical detent feedback.

notes: Two generations only, MY2002-2012, sold in the US as 'Liberty' (marketed as Cherokee outside North America). No 2013 model year: production ended August 2012 and the nameplate was retired, replaced for MY2014 by the unibody Cherokee (KL) — record that as a hard end, not a bridge. The KJ→KK boundary at 2007/2008 is unambiguous (body-on-frame-ish unibody carryover but new body, suspension and interior). Note the KK dropped both the four-cylinder and the diesel, so any 4-cyl or CRD complaint is necessarily KJ. The 2.8L VM Motori CRD diesel is a low-volume US variant (2005-2006) with its own failure profile and is worth a sub-page.

engines: 2.8L VM Motori CRD turbodiesel I4 (2005-2006 US)

known_issues.description: Front lower control arm ball joint wear and separation. NHTSA recalls covered vehicles built 2 Jan 2001 - 4 Oct 2002 (modified ball joint assemblies plus heat shields) and 5 Oct 2002 - 26 Mar 2003 (inspect/replace as necessary with heat shields). Heat from the exhaust degrading the joint boot was implicated.

Window regulator failure — the regulator binds, tips the glass forward, chatters, and the window drops into the door, often suddenly. Subject of a US class action alleging the defect spans the whole generation and cannot be permanently repaired.

engines: 3.7L PowerTech V6, 210 hp (only engine offered in the US)

known_issues.description: Totally Integrated Power Module (TIPM) failure — gauges dropping to zero with warning lights illuminating, no-start conditions, and fuel pump relay faults. Concentrated in the last two model years of the generation.
Sky Slider full-length retractable fabric roof jams, binds, tears, and makes noise; drain tubes clog and leak water into the cabin. Optional equipment, offered on early KK years.
Window regulator failures carry over from the KJ generation.

notes: Five generations touch the 1996-2025 NHTSA window. Boundaries are clean and platform-driven. Important trap: the Suburban did NOT switch to GMT800 with the 1999 Silverado — 1999 was the final GMT400 Suburban and the GMT800 Suburban arrived for MY2000, so a 1999 Suburban belongs with the old truck, not the new one. NHTSA 'SUBURBAN' covers both 1500 (half-ton) and 2500 (three-quarter-ton) trucks with materially different powertrains; the mainstream passenger version is the 1500, mapped here, with 2500-only engines noted. The MY2021 T1XX change is more than a platform rename: it replaced the solid rear axle with independent rear suspension, which changes the rear suspension/driveline failure profile entirely. GM dropped the 2500 Suburban after MY2013 and revived a heavy-duty Suburban HD only later, so 2500-specific engines are largely a pre-2014 phenomenon.

known_issues.description: Central Sequential Fuel Injection (CSFI/'spider') injector assembly on the 5.7L Vortec — the plastic poppet nozzles and supply lines crack and leak, causing hard starting, rough running, misfire and raw fuel intrusion. Affects the Vortec-era engines from the 1996 changeover onward.
Corrosion-driven brake and fuel line perforation in salt-belt states is a recurring late-life failure mode for this generation.

Instrument panel cluster gauge failure — the stepper motors driving the speedometer, tachometer, fuel and temperature gauges stick, flutter, or go dead. Not a safety recall but covered by GM Special Coverage Adjustment bulletin 07187 (7 years/70,000 miles) for 2003-2004 and certain 2005 vehicles; a defining defect of the late GMT800 years.
Fuel level sender/sending unit failure causing erratic or stuck fuel gauge readings, often confused with the cluster stepper motor fault.

engines: 5.3L LMG / LC9 (flex-fuel) Vortec V8 with Active Fuel Management

known_issues.description: Active Fuel Management (cylinder deactivation) valve lifter collapse on the Gen IV 5.3L V8 — the AFM lifter's locking pin fails, the lifter collapses, the camshaft lobe is wiped, and the engine misfires with progressive internal damage. Closely coupled to excessive oil consumption: the AFM oil pressure relief valve sprays oil at the piston skirts and the low-tension piston rings pass oil to the combustion chamber, fouling plugs and accelerating lifter failure. Worst on the flex-fuel LC9 variants. No safety recall was issued; repair typically requires cam and lifter replacement.
Dashboard top pad cracks and splits, typically radiating from the airbag seams and speaker grilles, with associated rattles. Widespread across the whole generation and a large ODI complaint category.

engines: 5.3L L83 EcoTec3 V8 with Active Fuel Management, 355 hp

known_issues.description: Active Fuel Management lifter failure continues on the 5.3L L83 — collapsed AFM lifter, wiped cam lobe, misfire on the deactivating cylinders (1, 4, 6, 7). Same mechanism as the GMT900 Gen IV engines.

Torque converter clutch shudder on GM's 8-speed and 10-speed automatics — a rumble-strip sensation at steady 40-70 mph cruise, caused by transmission fluid unable to maintain the required friction characteristics. GM's remedy is a fluid flush to Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP per TSB 18-NA-355; where the flush fails the torque converter is replaced. Subject of class action litigation covering GM's 8-speed applications.

engines: 5.3L L84 EcoTec3 V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management
6.2L L87 EcoTec3 V8 with Dynamic Fuel Management

known_issues.description: 6.2L L87 V8 connecting rod and crankshaft manufacturing defects causing bearing damage, engine knock, and catastrophic engine failure with loss of propulsion. NHTSA recall 25V-274 (April 2025) covers roughly 598,000 US vehicles including Suburban; remedy is inspection and, where indicated, engine replacement plus a switch to heavier-weight oil. GM has stated this recall is separate from the long-running valve lifter complaints.

Dynamic Fuel Management lifter failure on both the L84 5.3L and L87 6.2L — the DFM lifter locking mechanism fails, collapsing the lifter and damaging the camshaft. Widely reported by owners; distinct from the 25V-274 rod/crank recall.

First Suburban generation with independent rear suspension, replacing the live axle. Rear suspension and air-ride (optional Air Ride Adaptive) failure modes have no analogue in earlier generations, so do not carry over pre-2021 rear-end failure patterns.

notes: The critical fact for this nameplate is the seven-model-year gap: US Ranger production ended 16 December 2011 at Twin Cities Assembly, with 2011 the last retail model year and a small 2012 fleet-only run; there is NO 2013-2018 US Ranger. Do not bridge that gap — the pre-gap truck is a compact body-on-frame Ranger with Ford US roots, and the post-gap truck is the global T6 Ranger, a midsize truck sharing nothing with it. Complaints keyed to 2013-2018 in the ODI data under 'RANGER' are almost certainly the Ranger EV, grey-market, or data errors and should be quarantined. Also note the 2019-2023 P375 and 2024+ P703 are genuinely different platforms despite similar appearance: P703 is a re-engineered chassis with a wider track, new frame and a V6 option, so keep them separate. The 1998-2011 third generation is unusually long (14 model years) and had a major mid-generation powertrain change — the 4.0L switched from OHV to SOHC for 2001 — which materially changes the failure profile within one generation.

known_issues.description: A4LD 4-speed automatic durability — overdrive and forward clutch failure, and torque converter lockup faults, are the characteristic transmission failure of the pre-5R55E trucks.
Salt-belt corrosion of the frame, cab corners and bed, typical of the era; late-life structural rust is a common ODI theme for these trucks.

Takata frontal airbag inflators. The 2004-2006 Ranger carries the highest-risk inflator population outside the Ranger's own class: Ford issued a do-not-drive advisory for vehicles with open recalls 15S21, 17S42 and 19S01, and NHTSA issued urgent consumer warnings after fatalities in these trucks. Both driver and passenger inflators are implicated; propellant degradation causes the inflator housing to rupture and spray metal fragments.

4.0L SOHC V6 timing chain cassette failure. The engine uses three chains with plastic guide cassettes and hydraulic tensioners; the guides embrittle and break, producing the characteristic cold-start rattle from the rear of the engine. Left unrepaired the chain can jump time or break, destroying the engine. The rear cassette is behind the engine, so the repair requires engine removal. Ford made incremental design improvements through roughly 2005, after which failures drop off markedly.

engines: 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharged I4, 270 hp — the only engine offered

known_issues.description: 10R80 10-speed harsh and erratic shifting — jerking, lunging, clunking and hesitation between gears, with slipping, shuddering and loss of power in worse cases. Root cause in earlier 10R80 builds is a poorly retained bushing in the CDF (Clutch D-F) drum that slides out of position and lets the Teflon sealing ring fail, dropping hydraulic pressure. Addressed through repeated Ford TSBs including TSB 24-2046, and the subject of class action litigation covering Ford's 10R80 applications.

build_notes: n/a: Too new for a settled systemic failure record as of the 2025 model year; complaint volume is dominated by early-build electrical and infotainment items rather than an established mechanical defect. Do not carry P375 findings across — the frame, track width and V6 powertrain options are new.

notes: Two traps in this nameplate. (1) MY2012 is a split year: the redesigned N17 sedan launched as a 2012 model while Nissan continued selling the old C11 hatchback as a 2012 model alongside it. I have assigned 2012 to the N17 because the sedan is the mainstream, higher-volume car, but a 2012 hatchback complaint is a first-generation vehicle. (2) The hatchback body split off under a separate nameplate — Versa Note (E12 chassis), US MY2014-2019 — which NHTSA generally files under its own model string 'VERSA NOTE'. It shares the HR16DE engine and Jatco JF015E CVT with the N17 sedan, so its failure profile belongs with the second generation, but I have not listed it as its own generation row to keep the ranges non-overlapping. There was no US Versa hatchback for MY2013. The Versa was discontinued for the US after MY2025 (production ended December 2025), so 2025 is the true end. The CVT is the single dominant failure mode across all three generations and is the obvious failure-mode hub page for this nameplate.

known_issues.description: Xtronic CVT overheating, shuddering, hesitation and premature failure. Nissan extended CVT coverage to 10 years/120,000 miles across its 2007-2010 CVT-equipped vehicles in response to widespread failures. Belt and pulley wear generates metal debris that contaminates the valve body.

Jatco JF015E (CVT7) failure — shuddering, juddering, hesitation, delayed engagement, overheating and outright failure, frequently just past the 60-month/60,000-mile powertrain warranty. The metal belt and pulleys wear prematurely, and the resulting shavings contaminate the valve body and stepper motor; DTC P0746 (pressure control solenoid performance) is the signature code. A class action over the 2012-2017 Versa CVT settled in late 2019, and in May 2020 Nissan launched a quality action extending CVT coverage to 84 months/84,000 miles for the 2012-2017 Versa sedan and 2014-2017 Versa Note.

Continued CVT complaints — shuddering, juddering, surging, jerking, delayed acceleration and episodes of unexpected hard acceleration. Nissan TSB NTB19-040d (August 2020) addresses reduced power and hesitation on the 2020 Versa sedan. Unlike the N17, the 2020-2023 Versa/Sentra CVT complaints have not reached a class settlement, so warranty relief is narrower.

notes: Three generations, all clean boundaries. The second generation is exceptionally long — fifteen model years, 2007-2021 — so within-generation segmentation matters more than usual for this nameplate: the V8 lineup changed twice (4.7L 2UZ-FE dropped after 2009, 4.6L 1UR-FE added 2010 and dropped after 2019), and there was a significant 2014 facelift with a new body and interior that owners often mistake for a new generation. It is not: the platform, frame and powertrains carried over. The first generation is a genuinely smaller truck than the ones that followed (it was closer to a large compact than a true half-ton), which distorts cross-generation comparisons. Toyota's US Tundra history is bracketed by two major engine/structure programs — frame corrosion at the start and the V35A twin-turbo bearing failures at the end.

known_issues.description: Frame corrosion and perforation. Toyota recalled roughly 110,000 MY2000-2003 Tundras across 20 cold-weather states and DC for frame rust that could allow the spare tire carrier to separate from the vehicle and, in advanced cases, compromise frame integrity. Inspection criteria centered on rust-through holes larger than about 10 mm; qualifying trucks received frame replacement. Toyota subsequently extended corrosion warranty coverage to later first-generation trucks.

Secondary air injection (AI) pump and air switching valve failure on the V8s. Moisture and exhaust condensate corrode the pump and valves, triggering check engine lights and limp/fail-safe mode. Toyota issued a Customer Support Program / warranty enhancement covering 2007-2010 Tundra air pump assemblies and air switching valves, and separately addressed a 2012-2014 Tundra ECM software condition that could itself cause the air injection pump to fail and put the truck into fail-safe mode.

Cam tower oil leaks on the 5.7L 3UR-FE — the sealant between the cam towers and cylinder head degrades and weeps oil, commonly presenting as oil in the spark plug tubes or a leak at the front of the engine. Labor-intensive repair requiring cam cover and timing cover disassembly.

engines: 3.4L V35A-FTS twin-turbo V6 hybrid (i-Force Max), 437 hp combined

known_issues.description: V35A-FTS main bearing failure from machining debris. Debris left in the block during machining was not fully cleared at assembly; under load it migrates to the main bearings, causing bearing wear, engine knock, power loss and in the worst cases a stall. Toyota's recall campaign initially covered 2022-2023 Tundra and Lexus LX with a free engine replacement remedy, and was later expanded — adding more than 127,000 vehicles and extending to 2022-2024 Tundra and 2022-2024 Lexus LX, after the original remedy proved insufficient.

First Tundra generation on the TNGA-F frame with a coil-spring (and optional air) rear suspension replacing leaf springs on some configurations; rear suspension failure patterns do not carry over from the XK50.

notes: Two things a naive year-range map gets wrong. (1) There is NO US 2014 model year Fit: the second generation ran long through MY2013 and the third generation arrived early as a MY2015 car, leaving a one-year hole. The only 2014-badged Fit in the US was the Fit EV, a separate lease-only compliance vehicle with a different powertrain that should not be merged into either gasoline generation. (2) The US start is offset from the global Fit — the first generation Fit had been on sale in Japan since 2001, but US sales began in April 2006 as a MY2007 car, so the US first generation is only two model years long and represents a late, facelifted portion of the GD run. The Fit was discontinued in the US after MY2020, replaced in the lineup by the HR-V; the global fourth-generation Fit (GR) was never sold in the US.

known_issues.description: Takata airbag inflator recalls, including a later campaign covering passenger frontal inflators installed as recall remedy or replacement service parts. Propellant degradation after long-term exposure to high humidity and temperature cycling can cause the inflator to rupture and spray metal fragments into the cabin.
Takata frontal airbag inflator recalls span this generation, part of Honda's multi-campaign Takata remediation.
Tailgate/hatch handle failure — the exterior release handle breaks or the microswitch fails, preventing the hatch from opening. A recurring, generation-specific complaint.
Front axle/CV shaft failures and premature front suspension wear are commonly reported for this generation.
Clear coat delamination and peeling, reported by owners from roughly 70,000 miles onward, concentrated in the earliest model year.

engines: 1.5L L15B1 DOHC i-VTEC I4 with direct injection, 130 hp

known_issues.description: VTC (variable timing control) actuator rattle — a distinct metallic rattle from the front of the engine for one to two seconds at cold start, caused by the actuator's locking pin failing to hold. Well documented across the generation.
CVT start-clutch judder — shudder and hesitation during low-speed engagement from a stop, attributed to premature clutch pack wear; in worse cases delayed acceleration and failure.

Direct-injection carbon buildup on the intake valves, presenting as misfire and rough running; combined with fuel injector and ignition coil faults this makes the engine the leading complaint category for the generation.

No-start conditions traced to the start/stop switch and starter motor, plus intermittent right-side instrument cluster display faults. Launch-year quality was notably weak, with multiple software-related recalls on the MY2015 car.

notes: US model years run 2010-2024. The Forte was replaced by the Kia K4 for MY2025 as part of Kia's global K-nomenclature realignment, so there is no US 2025 Forte — the 2025 records in the ODI extract are almost certainly stray, mis-keyed, or Canadian-market carryover and should not force a 2025 boundary. The Forte replaced the Kia Spectra in 2010, so the nameplate does not extend below 2010. Body-style coverage varies by generation and is worth capturing: gen 1 offered sedan, Koup coupe and Forte5 hatchback; gen 2 offered all three but dropped the Koup after MY2016; gen 3 is sedan-only in the US (the hatchback was not sold here). Source disagreement to note: some recall summaries describe the KSDS knock-sensor campaign as covering '2012-2015 Forte with the 2.0 Nu engine', but the Kia engine class settlement documentation indicates the Forte used Theta II engines through MY2013 and moved to the Nu family for MY2014. I have followed the settlement documentation, which is the more authoritative source, and flag the discrepancy here.

known_issues.description: No engine immobilizer on keyed-ignition trims. Vehicles started with a steel key can be hot-wired via the steering column ignition cylinder, the basis of the widely publicized 'Kia Challenge' theft wave. Kia's remedy is a dealer-installed anti-theft software upgrade or, for ineligible vehicles, a physical theft deterrent device. Immobilizers became standard from MY2022.

Theta II engine connecting rod bearing wear leading to knock and seizure is the family-level defect for Kia's Theta II engines and is covered by the Kia engine class settlement; the Forte and Forte Koup 2.4L Theta II MPI applications fall within that settlement's scope.

engines: 1.6L Gamma T-GDI turbo I4, 201 hp (Forte5 SX / Koup SX)

known_issues.description: 2.0L Nu connecting rod bearing wear. Kia's remedy is the Knock Sensor Detection System (KSDS) software campaign, which monitors engine vibration for the onset of excessive rod bearing wear and alerts the driver at an early stage — before bearing failure progresses to seizure or an engine compartment fire. Delivered as a free dealer software update.
Keyed-ignition trims lack an engine immobilizer, leaving them vulnerable to the same steering-column hot-wire theft method as the first generation. Eligible for Kia's anti-theft software upgrade.

engines: 1.6L Gamma II T-GDI turbo I4, 201 hp (GT)

known_issues.description: Keyed-ignition trims through MY2021 lack an engine immobilizer and are within the Kia theft-vulnerability population; immobilizers became standard equipment from MY2022, so 2022-2024 Fortes are not affected.

IVT (Kia's continuously variable transmission, introduced on this generation) draws hesitation, shudder and delayed-engagement complaints, concentrated in the early years before calibration revisions.

notes: The single most important fact for this nameplate is the MY2017 overlap: two completely unrelated vehicles were sold in US showrooms as '2017 Jeep Compass'. A short run of the old MK Compass was built through December 2016 and titled as MY2017, while the all-new MP Compass went on sale in spring 2017. They share essentially nothing — the MK is a heavily modified Mitsubishi-derived platform with a CVT, the MP is a Fiat Small Wide 4x4 platform with a 9-speed automatic. Because the ranges must not overlap I have assigned 2017 to the MP (the far higher-volume car for that model year), but complaint records keyed to MY2017 must be VIN-disambiguated before being attributed, or the MK carryover units will silently pollute the MP page. The old MK Compass can be identified by its Patriot-like body and CVT. A third generation (J4U, STLA-platform) has been announced but its North American launch has slipped and it does not appear in the 2007-2025 data window.

known_issues.description: Jatco JF011E (CVT2) overheating, slipping, shuddering and premature failure. Fluid breaks down under heat stress, the pulleys wear and the belt slips; the transmission drops into limp mode and fails, commonly between roughly 60,000 and 95,000 miles when fluid service is neglected. A US class action specifically targeted the 2010-2013 cars.
2.0L/2.4L World engine excessive oil consumption and top-end ticking are recurring complaints across the generation.
TIPM (Totally Integrated Power Module) faults consistent with the wider Chrysler TIPM population of the era — no-start, stall, and unrelated multi-system electrical symptoms.

2.4L Tigershark excessive oil consumption — owners report losing roughly a quart per 1,000 miles. FCA issued Customer Satisfaction Notifications attributing part of the consumption to the Interactive Deceleration Fuel ShutOff (IDFSO) calibration, which cuts fuel on deceleration and creates cylinder vacuum that draws oil past the rings; piston ring and bore issues are also implicated. Same defect family as the 2015-2017 Chrysler 200 and Jeep Renegade/Cherokee 2.4L applications.

ZF 948TE 9-speed rough and harsh shifting, lurching, and hesitation — the most-reported complaint category for the generation. The MP shares its calibration history and TSB software flashes with the Cherokee KL; a related wiring harness defect in the 9-speed family can cause sudden shutdown or unexpected shifts into neutral.
Launch-year electrical and infotainment faults were notably concentrated in the first two model years of the generation.

notes: Five generations touch the 1996-2025 window; boundaries are chassis-code driven and well established. The complication is body styles running past the sedan's generation change, producing two real overlaps that a pure sedan-based map hides. (1) The W204 coupe (C204) was sold in the US as MY2012-2015, so 2015 contains both a W204 coupe and a W205 sedan. (2) The W205 coupe and cabriolet (C205/A205) continued in the US through MY2023, so 2022-2023 contains both W205 coupes/cabrios and W206 sedans; they were replaced by the CLE (C236/A236) for MY2024, not by a W206 coupe. I have mapped the sedan lineage to keep ranges contiguous and non-overlapping per the brief, and record the coupe/cabrio spans here — a MY2015 coupe complaint is W204 hardware, and a MY2022-2023 coupe complaint is W205 hardware. Also note the US start: the W202 reached the US for MY1994, so the 1996 floor of the data window sits mid-generation. The C-Class is a family nameplate spanning four-cylinder economy sedans and M156/M177 AMG V8s; the AMG variants have their own distinct failure profiles and warrant separate treatment.

engines: 2.3L M111 I4 and supercharged Kompressor (C230 / C230K, 1997-2000)

known_issues.description: Biodegradable wiring harness insulation degradation. Mercedes used a soy/cellulose-based insulation on engine and interior harnesses in the mid-1990s; it embrittles, cracks and flakes off, producing shorts, phantom fault codes, rough running and no-start conditions. Affects the earliest W202 build years and is the defining electrical failure of the generation.
Evaporator and A/C system failures — leaking evaporators and condensers and compressor failure, a labor-intensive dash-out repair.
Water-based paint delamination and clear coat failure, plus corrosion at the wheel arches, jack points and door bottoms, characteristic of Mercedes builds of this era.

M272 V6 balance shaft sprocket premature wear. The sprocket and the timing chain idler gear were made from insufficiently hardened material; as the teeth wear, camshaft timing drifts relative to the crankshaft, setting fault codes P1200/P1208 with rough running and a check engine light. Affects engines built from roughly 2004 through September 2006 — in the C-Class that means the MY2006-2007 C280 and C350. Repair requires engine removal and typically runs $3,800-$5,000.
M271 supercharged I4 single-row timing chain stretch, with consequent wear of the camshaft adjuster sprockets and adjuster solenoid faults. Presents as rattle, timing codes and rough running.

SAM (Signal Acquisition Module) failure — a single failed module produces a scattered set of symptoms: dead fuel gauge, lights inoperative, repeated fuse failures, key fob non-recognition, battery drain, rear lights staying on, and unresponsive dashboard controls. Frequently misdiagnosed as multiple independent faults.
722.6 automatic jerky and delayed gear changes progressing to complete shift failure, commonly traced to the conductor plate and valve body.
M272 V6 balance shaft sprocket wear carries into the early years of this generation on engines built before the material change, causing timing drift and P1200/P1208 codes; engine-out repair.
M271 EVO turbocharged I4 timing chain and camshaft adjuster wear, with adjuster magnet/solenoid faults producing rattle, timing codes and rough running.
M156 6.2L V8 (C63 AMG) head bolt corrosion and failure, and camshaft lobe/lifter wear, both well documented on early M156 builds. AMG-specific — do not generalize to the mainstream C300/C350.

generations.platform_code: W205 (S205 wagon, C205 coupe, A205 cabriolet)
engines: 3.0L M276 biturbo V6 (C400 / C450 / AMG C43)
4.0L M177 biturbo V8 (AMG C63 / C63 S)

known_issues.description: M274 2.0L turbo wrist pin and piston issues on early C300 builds, presenting as knocking or ticking under load.
Rapid battery discharge and parasitic drain, particularly on vehicles left standing; a leading no-start cause for the generation. Keyless-Go module faults typically appear around 40,000-60,000 km.
COMAND infotainment freezes, reboots and display faults, concentrated in pre-facelift cars and often appearing within the first 30,000 km.
Door handle sensor and LED failures (typically 60,000-80,000 km), sagging sunroof shades, and interior trim noise.
Airmatic air suspension failures on so-equipped cars — compressor and air strut leaks causing ride height loss.

engines: 2.0L M254 turbocharged I4 with 48V integrated starter-generator mild hybrid (C300)
2.0L M139l turbocharged I4 with electric exhaust gas turbocharger and 48V system (AMG C43)

known_issues.description: 48V mild-hybrid integrated starter-generator and belt-alternator-starter system faults are the emerging complaint theme for this generation, presenting as no-start, warning messages and loss of the electric assist. Too recent for a settled long-term failure record — treat findings as provisional and do not carry W205 patterns across, as the powertrain electrification and MBUX architecture are both new.

Major generational change worth flagging even absent a defect record: the W206 dropped all six- and eight-cylinder engines from the mainstream and AMG C43 lineup in favor of electrified four-cylinders. Any cross-generation reliability comparison against W205 V6/V8 cars is comparing different machines.

notes: Single generation only — the G6 existed for six model years (2005-2010) and was killed when GM wound down Pontiac. Replaced the Pontiac Grand Am. The mid-2009 '2009.5' revision (new front/rear fascias, revised dash, Bluetooth radio) is a facelift on the same Epsilon platform, NOT a new generation; some data sources list a '2009.5' model year that should be folded into 2009. Body styles: sedan, coupe, and a retractable-hardtop convertible — all one generation. Mechanical twins for cross-referencing failure modes: Chevrolet Malibu (2004-2012), Saturn Aura (2007-2010), Saab 9-3. Verified against Wikipedia and the Cars.com NHTSA recall list. NOTE: I checked whether the G6 was in GM's 2014 'unintended ignition key rotation' recall 14V-400 — it was NOT (that campaign covered Impala, Monte Carlo, Malibu 1997-2005, Alero, Intrigue, Grand Am, Grand Prix). Do not attach the ignition-switch story to G6 pages.

known_issues.description: Sudden loss of electric power steering assist while driving, caused by a fault in the EPS torque sensor assembly; steering reverts to unassisted manual effort, worst at low speed. Remedy was replacement of the torque sensor assembly. NHTSA campaign 14V-153; expanded by 15V-064 for a further build window.

Increased electrical resistance at the Body Control Module connection produces voltage fluctuations that can disable brake lamps, cruise control, traction control/StabiliTrak and other crash-avoidance functions. NHTSA campaign 14V-252.

The tabs on the automatic transmission shift cable end can fracture and separate, so the shifter position no longer matches the gear actually engaged — the car can be shifted to PARK and the key removed while the transmission is still in gear, allowing rollaway. NHTSA campaign 12V-460.
Shift cable adjustment clip may not be fully seated, producing a mismatch between indicated and actual gear position. NHTSA campaign 09V-073.
Timing chain wear/stretch producing cold-start rattle and cam/crank correlation codes, and elevated oil consumption; aggravated by extended oil change intervals.

notes: CRITICAL: the Pacifica nameplate covers two completely unrelated vehicles with a 8-model-year gap between them. Gen 1 (2004-2008) is a CS-platform car-based crossover/wagon. There was NO Pacifica for model years 2009-2016 — record this gap explicitly, do not bridge it. Gen 2 (2017-present) is an RU-platform minivan that replaced the Town & Country and shares nothing but the name. Wikipedia keeps them as two separate articles and calls the minivan a 'first generation' in its own right; for a generation-keyed site the cleanest scheme is Gen 1 = crossover, Gen 2 = minivan, with the gap stated on both pages. The 2021 minivan facelift (new front end, Pinnacle trim) is NOT a new generation — same RU platform. AWD was added to the gas minivan for MY2020. The Pacifica Hybrid (plug-in) uses a completely different drivetrain (eFlite EVT, high-voltage LG battery) and carries its own defect set — worth a sub-page. Note also the 2021-2023 'Chrysler Voyager' is the decontented RU sibling and may appear under a separate NHTSA model string.

known_issues.description: A broken retaining pin on the rocker arm shaft blocks the oil passage, producing a loud top-end ticking noise and eventual valvetrain wear. Affects the 3.5L, 3.8L and 4.0L V6 across the whole run; the single most-reported engine complaint for this generation.

Failure of the externally mounted input/output speed sensors and of the solenoid pack, dropping the transmission into limp mode (locked in 2nd gear) with a P0700 stored. Common enough that P0700 is the signature code for this platform.
Front engine cradle corrodes and can split apart in salt-belt states, in severe cases allowing the powertrain to drop. A structural rust failure mode, not a wear item.
Carbon buildup on the intake valves of the 3.5L and 4.0L V6 causing misfires and check-engine lights.

engines: 3.6L Atkinson-cycle Pentastar V6 + dual-motor hybrid drive, plug-in (Pacifica Hybrid, 2017-2025)
transmissions: eFlite electrically variable transmission — dual motor EVT (Hybrid/PHEV)

known_issues.description: Abrupt engine stall and loss of power steering assist traced to improperly installed/routed wiring; recall covered roughly 198,700 gasoline Pacificas. A separate recall attributed stalling to a powertrain control module defect on 2018 vehicles.

An internal transmission wiring connector can short circuit, causing unexpected engine shutdown/stall, most often above 25 mph. Recall covered roughly 67,000-76,000 Pacifica Hybrids; remedy was a power inverter software update plus, where needed, an instrument cluster software update. NHTSA later opened a recall-query investigation into whether the software remedy was adequate.

Fire risk from the LG-supplied high-voltage battery pack while parked and charging; roughly 20,000 vehicles recalled after 12 owner fire reports, with owners told to park outside and away from structures and to stop charging. Same cell supplier implicated in the Chevrolet Bolt and Hyundai Kona EV battery recalls.

Early shift-quality complaints — harsh or delayed engagement, hunting between ratios — addressed through repeated TCM/PCM calibration updates rather than hardware. Characteristic of FCA's early 9HP applications.
Separate recalls on 2018 vehicles for a seat belt that can become unlatched and for a front axle defect.

notes: ONE generation across the entire 2009-2020 run — an unusually long single-generation life (12 model years). The 2011 model year brought a very heavy mid-cycle overhaul: new grille and lower fascia, completely redesigned interior, retuned suspension and steering, LED tail lamps, new Dodge logo, and — most important for failure analysis — the switch from the 3.5L SOHC V6 to the 3.6L Pentastar V6 with the 62TE 6-speed. That is a facelift on the same JC49 platform, NOT a new generation, but 2009-2010 and 2011-2020 should be treated as distinct powertrain cohorts on any failure-mode page. The 2.4L four-cylinder kept a 4-speed automatic for the entire production run, right through 2020. Marketed abroad as the Fiat Freemont; shares FCA's D-segment platform with the Dodge Avenger and the wheelbase of the short-wheelbase Chrysler minivan.

known_issues.description: Premature valve guide wear in the left (driver's side) cylinder head causes a distinct ticking noise from the driver's side of the engine bay, progressing to misfires on cylinders 2/4/6 (P0302, P0304, P0306) and a check-engine light. Chrysler extended the cylinder head warranty on affected Journeys to 10 years / 150,000 miles from in-service date.
known_issues.affected_years: 2011-2013 (head redesigned after; some sources extend symptom reports to 2015)

known_issues.description: Failure of the integrated fuse/relay module, classically a stuck or failed fuel pump relay, causing crank-no-start, stalling while driving, and assorted phantom electrical faults. One of the defining FCA defects of this era.
known_issues.affected_years: 2011-2013 most heavily reported; module used across the run

known_issues.description: The plastic oil filter housing/oil cooler assembly cracks and leaks, and the integral oil by-pass valve can fail. Signs are oil leakage down the front of the engine and low oil pressure warnings.
Debris collecting in the cylinder head coolant passages is among the most frequently reported Journey engine faults in aggregated repair data.

The carryover 4-speed automatic paired with the 2.4L for the model's entire life draws consistent harsh-shift and durability complaints; it was never updated even as the V6 moved to the 6-speed 62TE in 2011.

notes: Three generations, contiguous, no gaps. Gen 1 (2008-2017) is a GM Lambda crossover, sibling to the GMC Acadia, Saturn Outlook and Chevrolet Traverse — failure modes are shared across all four and should cross-link. Gen 1 received a 2013 mid-cycle refresh (new fascias, interior, front center airbag) plus a change from the 3.6L LLT to the 3.6L LFX engine; that is a facelift, not a new generation, but 2008-2012 vs 2013-2017 are meaningfully different reliability cohorts because the worst timing-chain years are in the first half. Gen 2 (2018-2024) moved to GM's C1XX (Chi) architecture and the 9-speed automatic. Gen 3 arrived for MY2025 on an updated C1 architecture with a 2.5L turbocharged four replacing the V6 — a complete powertrain break, and far too new for meaningful complaint data. Gen 1's first model year is 2008 (on sale June 2008 as a 2008 MY vehicle), so the NHTSA span starting at 2008 is correct.

engines: 3.6L LLT DOHC V6, direct injection, 288 hp (2009-2012)
3.6L LFX DOHC V6, direct injection, 288-310 hp (2013-2017)

known_issues.description: Premature timing chain stretch on the 3.6L LY7/LLT. Symptoms are a rattle on cold start, rough idle, power loss and cam/crank correlation codes P0008/P0016/P0017/P0018; a chain that jumps teeth can destroy the engine. GM attributed a large share of it to the original Oil Life Monitor calibration permitting excessively long oil change intervals, which degraded the oil feeding the hydraulic tensioners. Addressed via multiple TSBs, a revised chain design, updated OLM software, and Special Coverage program #11340 extending coverage to 10 years / 120,000 miles.

Fracture of the 3-5-Reverse wave plate inside the 6-speed automatic. The vehicle abruptly loses 3rd gear, 5th gear and Reverse — it revs without moving or feels like it is slipping. Requires transmission teardown; the single most notorious driveline failure of this generation.

known_issues.component: Fuel system — high pressure fuel pump (direct injection)
known_issues.description: HPFP and direct-injection fueling faults on the LLT, often surfacing alongside the timing chain wear because both are driven off the camshafts.
Missing bolts on the start/stop accumulator endcap can allow a transmission oil leak that progresses to loss of propulsion. GM recall covering 2019-2020 vehicles.

Rough shifting, shudder and hesitation under acceleration, and a 2-1 downshift clunk when slowing; commonly addressed with a TCM software reflash rather than hardware. Fluid degradation is reported to contribute from roughly 55,000 miles.
Brake booster failures reported, in some cases repeatedly on the same vehicle, around the 100,000-mile mark; brakes are among the top complaint categories for this generation.

notes: The single most dangerous model in this batch for naming collisions. Three separate NHTSA model strings overlap: (a) 'SANTA FE', (b) 'SANTA FE SPORT', (c) 'SANTA FE XL'. For the 3rd generation (DM/NC), Hyundai sold a short-wheelbase 5-seater badged 'Santa Fe Sport' (2013-2018) and a long-wheelbase 7-seater badged simply 'Santa Fe' (2013-2018) — then for MY2019 the LWB car was renamed 'Santa Fe XL' and the all-new TM 4th-generation 5-seater took over the plain 'Santa Fe' name. CONSEQUENCE: model year 2019 contains BOTH a 3rd-generation DM (badged Santa Fe XL) and a 4th-generation TM (badged Santa Fe). Any grouping keyed on model name + year alone will merge them. Recommend routing MY2013-2018 'SANTA FE' records to the DM long-wheelbase page, MY2013-2018 'SANTA FE SPORT' to the DM short-wheelbase page, MY2019 'SANTA FE XL' to the DM LWB page, and MY2019+ plain 'SANTA FE' to the TM page. Also note the engine defect story splits by engine, not by trim: the Theta II four-cylinders carry the rod-bearing/fire actions; the 3.3L Lambda V6 in the long-wheelbase cars does not. Generations are otherwise contiguous with no production gaps.

known_issues.description: Automatic transmission failure is the dominant durability complaint for this generation; no manufacturer recall campaign, so it appears in complaint data rather than recall data.

The 2.4L Theta II introduced here belongs to the engine family later subject to the connecting-rod bearing failure actions. IMPORTANT PRECISION: Hyundai's engine recalls concentrated on the GDI (direct-injection) Theta II from MY2013 onward; the 2010-2012 Santa Fe's port-injected 2.4L Theta II is not the primary recall population. State the family relationship, not a recall, on this page.

known_issues.component: Engine — Theta II GDI connecting rod bearings
known_issues.description: Machining debris left in the crankshaft oil passages during manufacturing restricts oil flow to the connecting rod bearings; the bearings wear, the engine develops a knock, then seizes — producing stalling while driving and, in some cases, engine compartment fires. Remedies included engine inspection/replacement and installation of the Knock Sensor Detection System (KSDS) software, which detects the onset of bearing wear and puts the vehicle into limp mode. NHTSA campaign 17V-226 covered MY2013-2014 Santa Fe Sport, with later expansions.
known_issues.affected_years: 2013-2018 Santa Fe Sport (2.0T and 2.4 GDI). Does NOT affect the 3.3L V6 long-wheelbase models.

known_issues.description: The anti-lock brake control module can suffer an internal electrical short, causing an engine compartment fire whether the vehicle is parked or driving. Owners were told to park outside and away from structures pending repair. One campaign covered 151,205 Santa Fe Sports built 17 June 2013 to 13 May 2015; a later separate campaign covered roughly 44,000 MY2018 Santa Fe Sports. Remedies involved module inspection plus multi-fuse installation.

The 2019-2020 carryover 2.4L GDI and 2.0T remain in the Theta II family covered by Hyundai's knock sensor detection system software campaigns for connecting-rod bearing wear. The 2021 switch to the Smartstream 2.5L is a clean powertrain break within the generation.
Drivability complaints (low-speed shudder, hesitation from a stop, jerky engagement) with the wet DCT paired to the 2.5L turbo introduced in the 2021 facelift.

generations.mixed_year_note: Both the outgoing and incoming generation were sold in this model year; NHTSA records do not separate them.

notes: IMPORTANT BOUNDARY DETAIL: there is no MY2008 Murano in the US. The Z50 ended after MY2007 and the Z51 launched as a MY2009 vehicle, so model year 2008 is empty — a one-year gap inside the nameplate. Do not let a 2003-2008/2009-2014 split leak Z51 cars into the Z50 page. The Murano CrossCabriolet (2011-2014) is a Z51 derivative and may appear under its own NHTSA model string. The dominant failure story across the first three generations is the JATCO CVT, and the specific mechanism differs by generation, so the failure-mode hub should be split, not merged. Gen 4 (Z53, MY2025) abandons the CVT entirely for a 9-speed torque-converter automatic and a VC-Turbo four — a complete break that resets the CVT narrative.

known_issues.description: Early-generation JATCO CVT failures: judder, delayed or absent engagement, loss of drive. Nissan extended the CVT warranty to 10 years / 120,000 miles on 2003-2010 CVT-equipped vehicles following a class action, which is the clearest public acknowledgment of the defect scope.

transmissions: JATCO Xtronic CVT (1st-gen unit early, 2nd-gen JATCO CVT from roughly 2010)

known_issues.description: Continued CVT failures. On the 2nd-generation JATCO unit the most commonly cited single root cause is failure of the flow control valve in the front pump — one estimate attributes up to 90% of failures to that part. Downstream, overheated fluid lets the steel belt slip against the pulleys, shedding metal debris through the unit. Symptoms: judder, delayed acceleration, sudden loss of power.
Reports of spontaneous shattering of the panoramic sunroof glass, a complaint pattern shared across several Nissan models of this era.

engines: 2.5L QR25DER supercharged I4 hybrid (Murano Hybrid, 2016-2017, limited availability)

known_issues.description: CVT durability complaints continued into this generation. A class action settlement (Beaver v. Nissan North America) covering MY2015-2018 Murano extended the New Vehicle Limited Warranty as it applies to the transmission and provided reimbursement for owners who had already paid for qualifying CVT repairs or replacements.

notes: CRITICAL GAP: there was NO Camaro for model years 2003-2009 — a seven-year production hiatus after the 4th-generation F-body ended in 2002 and before the 5th-generation Zeta car arrived for MY2010. Record the gap explicitly; do not bridge 2002 to 2010. The supplied NHTSA complaint span (2010-2024) covers only the 5th and 6th generations, but the site's 1996-2025 window also touches the tail of the 4th generation (1996-2002), so I have mapped it. The 4th generation began in MY1993, before the site window. The Camaro was discontinued again after MY2024 — there is no MY2025 Camaro. Within the 6th generation the 2019 facelift (revised front fascia, wider adoption of the 10-speed automatic) is a facelift on the same Alpha platform, not a new generation.

known_issues.description: The LT1's Optispark optical distributor sits behind the water pump at the front of the engine, where coolant weep and moisture contaminate the optical sensor, causing misfires, stumbling and no-start. Replacement requires water pump removal, making it a costly and frequently repeated repair.
Intake manifold gasket degradation on GM's pushrod V6s of the period, producing coolant loss and oil/coolant intermixing.

engines: 6.2L LS3 V8, 426 hp (SS, manual) / 6.2L L99 V8, 400 hp (SS, automatic)

known_issues.description: Premature timing chain wear/stretch on the direct-injection 3.6L. The mechanism is a feedback loop: elevated oil consumption drops oil pressure to the hydraulic chain tensioners, the chain goes slack, stretches and can skip teeth. Symptoms begin with a cold-start rattle, then rough idle, power loss and cam/crank correlation codes.
known_issues.affected_years: 2010-2011 (LLT) most heavily reported; carries into early LFX

known_issues.description: Above-average oil consumption on the GM 3.6L, traced to PCV system faults and worn piston rings; directly aggravates the timing chain failure mode above.

GM recalled 2010-2014 Camaros because a driver's knee can contact the key fob and rotate the ignition switch out of RUN, cutting engine power, power steering and power braking and disabling airbag deployment. Remedy changed the key from a slotted to a hole-type design so the fob hangs closer to the steering column.

Slip-stick shudder from the torque converter clutch, felt as a vibration under light throttle at highway speed. GM determined the original factory-fill ATF was hygroscopic — it absorbed moisture from the air, changing the fluid's friction properties and glazing the TCC friction material. TSB 18-NA-355 prescribes a complete fluid exchange to the reformulated Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP (blue label) rather than converter replacement; if left unserviced the friction material burnishes and the torque converter must be replaced. Subject of multiple class actions.
known_issues.affected_years: 2016-2019 most heavily documented; unit used through 2024

notes: Clean, contiguous generations with no gaps. The one boundary that is very easy to get wrong is the 5th-to-6th transition: the 5th generation ran an exceptionally long 15 model years, 2010 through 2024 inclusive, and the 6th generation is a MY2025 vehicle. Toyota's own pressroom titles the transition 'Fifth (2010-2024) and Sixth (2025) Generations', which settles it — Wikipedia's production-year framing of '2024-present' for the 6th gen refers to calendar-year production start, not model year, and will mislead anyone mapping model years. The 2nd generation (N120/N130, MY1990-1995) falls just outside the site's 1996 window; the 3rd generation starts exactly at MY1996, so the NHTSA span aligns cleanly. Within the 5th generation the 2014 and 2020 facelifts are cosmetic/equipment updates on the same N280 platform, not new generations, though the 2020 addition of standard Toyota Safety Sense P matters for ADAS-related complaints.

known_issues.description: Lower ball joint wear and separation, which can allow the suspension to collapse and the wheel to fold under at speed. Toyota recalled 2001-2002 4Runners for the defect; owners note the same lower ball joint part number was used from 1996 through 2002 and report failures on earlier, non-recalled vehicles.

Severe frame rust, particularly at the rear of the frame rails and crossmembers, in salt-exposed regions. NHTSA received reports of steering and suspension components separating from a rusted-through frame.

Severe frame corrosion in salt-exposed regions that can compromise structural integrity. Toyota ran inspection campaigns for early 4th-generation vehicles and offered frame replacement or vehicle buyback for qualifying trucks.

engines: 4.0L 1GR-FE V6, 270 hp (sole engine for all 15 model years)

notes: IMPORTANT GAP: there is NO model year 2021 MDX in the US. The 3rd generation ended after MY2020 and the 4th generation launched as a MY2022 vehicle, skipping MY2021 entirely. Any 2014-2021 / 2022-present split will be wrong; record the empty year. The 3rd generation contains a mid-generation transmission change that matters more than the facelift: 6-speed automatic for MY2014-2015, ZF 9-speed for MY2016-2020, plus a 7-speed dual-clutch in the MDX Sport Hybrid (2017-2020) — three different transmissions inside one generation, so failure pages should be cut by transmission, not by generation.
